Yes. Yes. Let me say it again: Yes. After a horror show in Week 4 with my NFL picks , I got back on track in a big way this past week. I was 10-4-1 straight up and 9-6-1 against the spread. That brings my season record straight up to 48-30-1 and the ATS record to 34-43-2. The ATS mark will be a slow climb to get back above .500 after that really bad Week 3. But I felt good about the picks this week. Time to build some momentum. Two good weeks in a row? All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Seattle Seahawks (-3) at Denver Broncos Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Seahawks lost a tough one to the 49ers last week and now face a short week on the road against Denver. The Broncos ' offense has struggled, even with Sean Payton taking over as the play-caller. Bo Nix has to pick it up, but this is a tough defense to try and fix things. Seattle takes a tough road game. Pick: Seahawks 23, Broncos 17 Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) London on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Jaguars will have been in London for two weeks, which makes this a challenge for the Texans , who went this week. Houston won for the first time on the road last week and now their division chances probably rest on this game. The Jaguars were sloppy last week, which will get them back focused. Jaguars will win a tight one. Pick: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons (+3) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a horrible showing in Green Bay, in which the defense was shredded. But the Falcons lost in overtime to the Ravens and quarterback Michael Penix was hurt. He will likely play here, and that's a good thing since he can light up the Chicago defense. Falcons win it. Pick: Falcons 27, Bears 21 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns There is a chance that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be back for this game after missing last week with an ankle injury. Even if he isn't, I think the Ravens defense will be up to the task of slowing down the Browns offense. If Jackson is back, the Ravens offense will move the ball. Pick: Ravens 24, Browns 13 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts (-7) The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game. Pick: Colts 28, Titans 17 New York Jets at New England Patriots (-7.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Patriots have turned their season around with consecutive victories as Drake Maye has come alive. The Jets played better on defense against Cleveland last week with eight sacks, but this is a bigger challenge. Look for Maye to keep it going as the Pats win a third straight. Pick: Patriots 28, Jets 13 New Orleans Saints at New York Giants (+1.5) The Saints have lost three straight and have fallen to 1-4. They didn't play well against the Vikings last week, but this is a chance to get right. The Giants tied last week, but Jameis Winston played well. I think this will be about defenses. Giants in a close one. Pick: Giants 19, Saints 16 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense. Pick: Eagles 23, Panthers 20 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3) Both of these teams righted the ship a bit with victories last week. The Bucs badly needed it after losing their first four. Tampa Bay ran it with Bucky Irving to beat the Cowboys and I think they can do that here as well. The defense played better in that game and will limit Aaron Rodgers somewhat. Bucs win it. Pick: Bucs 26, Steelers 21 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams (-13.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The "Dream Team" Rams are 2-3 and haven't looked the part of a Super Bowl champ. The offense got it going against the Bills , but the defense was a non-factor in the fourth quarter and overtime. They will play better here against the Cardinals . Meanwhile, Matt Stafford will have a big day. Pick: Rams 35, Cardinals 20 Los Angeles Chargers (+8.5) at Kansas City Chiefs Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chargers limp into this one at 0-5, while the Chiefs are undefeated off a bye. The Chargers are desperate and need a win or their season will be over. This is not a good place to try to get that first victory. Look for Patrick Mahomes to play well. Chiefs coach Andy Reid is outstanding in his career off a bye. Pick: Chiefs 28, Chargers 21 Buffalo Bills (-6) at Las Vegas Raiders The Bills are playing consecutive road games, but they stayed on the West Coast after beating the Rams in overtime Monday night. That was a tough, physical game, which will make it a challenge on a short week. The Raiders were awful against the Pats, but they will play better on offense here. They just won't stop the Bills. Pick: Bills 35, Raiders 21 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Packers blew out the Bears Sunday as Jordan Love lit up the skies. Look for more of that in this one against a bad Dallas secondary. The Cowboys struggled on defense against the Bucs, and that will continue in this one. Love continues to play well. Packers win a shootout. Pick: Packers 31, Cowboys 27 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a long road trip for the Commanders off a brutal tie last week to face the league's best team right now. That's a tough combination. They can only hope for a letdown by the 49ers after they beat Seattle last week. It won't happen. The 49ers continue to roll as Brock Purdy continues to make a claim as a legitimate MVP candidate. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) at Denver Broncos (TNF) Dajani ( Seahawks -2.5): Through five weeks, I have only bet against the Denver Broncos once. It's an uncomfortable position to be in, since Bo Nix is "captain comeback." For example, I had zero doubt they would come back from down 16-0 against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3. Denver has the most comeback wins (15), second-half comebacks (12) and fourth-quarter comebacks (8) in the NFL since 2025. However, I'm going to fade the Broncos in this spot for a couple of reasons. One, Sean Payton taking back play-calling duties did not help anything against the Los Angeles Chargers . Getting this offense off the ground is, unfortunately, going to take some time -- and it probably won't happen against the No. 1 defense in the NFL. Secondly, the Seahawks have to be mad after that loss to the 49ers. Seattle has won five straight games following a loss, having not lost back-to-back games since 2024. The Seahawks have also won seven straight prime-time games, which is the longest active streak in the NFL. … Prediction: Seahawks 23, Broncos 20 Dubin (Seahawks -2.5): Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have resulted in the Broncos coming away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Patrick Surtain II here, which is obviously a problem against Jaxon Smith-Njigba . … Prediction: Seahawks 24, Broncos 16 Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was

away.headline: Broncos vs. Seahawks: 5 things Denver fans should know about Seattle
away.blurb: Sam's return has been shaky at best. It's odd, he looked rather fine in Week 3, which was essentially his first game since the Super Bowl (I'm not really counting the five plays he had in Week 1). Despite the two interceptions, Darnold did throw for 379 yards and four touchdown passes. In the two games since then, he has not cracked 200 yards, has only thrown for one touchdown each, and has thrown three more interceptions. He does not look comfortable in this offense for the last two weeks. He has shown a shocking lack of command and decisive action, which is concerningly showing itself in taking more sacks than usual. I still feel like these issues are correctable, but Denver is a tough draw to get back on track against. 1) How does Sam Darnold look after the injury suffered early in Week 1? 2) What role did ex- Broncos QB Drew Lock play in the early going of the ‘26 season? Drew Lock was exaclty what you want from a backup. He was solid, did not turn the ball over, and did more than enough to win the game. Seattle clearly trusts their primary backup, as he was not just a dink and dunker. They had enough faith to have him toss it deep plenty of times. Lock was already a "made man" when he upset the Eagles on MNF in 2023, but beating the Patriots on banner night this year minted him forever in the hearts of the 12th Man for the rest of time. 3) What is the biggest strength of the Seahawks right now? The biggest weakness? Their defensive line is easily their biggest strength. This unit is an absolute joy to watch as a fan, and I imagine would be a nightmare to play against. Leonard Williams is the best defensive tackle in the league, but don't overlook his running mate Byron Murphy II who had two sacks of the previously sackless Brock Purdy. Weakness? The Seahawks can't run the ball. They have two rushing touchdowns from running backs all year, and are not consistently dominating on the ground. Part of the reason is they are without both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price, who were/are the presumed starter/main backup. All respect to Emanuel Wilson, who is playing fine, he is a No. 3 not a No. 1. He is doing his best to hold down the fort, but outside of him they are getting little to no production from anyone else. 4) Name an underrated Seahawk that Broncos fans should know about going into Week 6? I mentioned Byron Murphy, but someone I also feel gets lost in the shuffle of Seattle's stellar defense is starting linebacker Ernest Jones IV. He is a two time Super Bowl champ and he led the NFL with linebacker interceptions last year, yet I don't feel like he gets the love he deserves. It always seems like when there is a big play, he is often involved. 5) Who wins, final score and why? I think Seattle gets back on track, at least when it comes to the win column. home.headline: Broncos vs. Seahawks: 5 things Denver fans should know about Seattle
home.blurb: Sam's return has been shaky at best. It's odd, he looked rather fine in Week 3, which was essentially his first game since the Super Bowl (I'm not really counting the five plays he had in Week 1). Despite the two interceptions, Darnold did throw for 379 yards and four touchdown passes. In the two games since then, he has not cracked 200 yards, has only thrown for one touchdown each, and has thrown three more interceptions. He does not look comfortable in this offense for the last two weeks. He has shown a shocking lack of command and decisive action, which is concerningly showing itself in taking more sacks than usual. I still feel like these issues are correctable, but Denver is a tough draw to get back on track against. 1) How does Sam Darnold look after the injury suffered early in Week 1? 2) What role did ex- Broncos QB Drew Lock play in the early going of the ‘26 season? Drew Lock was exaclty what you want from a backup. He was solid, did not turn the ball over, and did more than enough to win the game. Seattle clearly trusts their primary backup, as he was not just a dink and dunker. They had enough faith to have him toss it deep plenty of times. Lock was already a "made man" when he upset the Eagles on MNF in 2023, but beating the Patriots on banner night this year minted him forever in the hearts of the 12th Man for the rest of time. 3) What is the biggest strength of the Seahawks right now? The biggest weakness? Their defensive line is easily their biggest strength. This unit is an absolute joy to watch as a fan, and I imagine would be a nightmare to play against. Leonard Williams is the best defensive tackle in the league, but don't overlook his running mate Byron Murphy II who had two sacks of the previously sackless Brock Purdy. Weakness? The Seahawks can't run the ball. They have two rushing touchdowns from running backs all year, and are not consistently dominating on the ground. Part of the reason is they are without both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price, who were/are the presumed starter/main backup. All respect to Emanuel Wilson, who is playing fine, he is a No. 3 not a No. 1. He is doing his best to hold down the fort, but outside of him they are getting little to no production from anyone else. 4) Name an underrated Seahawk that Broncos fans should know about going into Week 6? I mentioned Byron Murphy, but someone I also feel gets lost in the shuffle of Seattle's stellar defense is starting linebacker Ernest Jones IV. He is a two time Super Bowl champ and he led the NFL with linebacker interceptions last year, yet I don't feel like he gets the love he deserves. It always seems like when there is a big play, he is often involved. 5) Who wins, final score and why? I think Seattle gets back on track, at least when it comes to the win column. Sam Darnold is turning the ball over too much and this offense is too one dimensional. But Seattle's defense is picking up plenty of the slack, and I haven't been overly impressed by Bo Nix

But the numbers beneath those records leave room for a considerably less predictable afternoon in London. Jacksonville enters as a 2.5-point favorite after escaping Philadelphia 19-17. Houston finally broke through by beating Tennessee 26-3, then acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. These predictions deliberately push beyond a narrow upset or another respectable quarterback performance. The forecast: Houston produces its most complete game of the season. CJ Stroud throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Jacksonville's defense allows only 14 points per game, second in the NFL. Predicting four passing touchdowns against that unit is aggressive, but its strength against the run can obscure a vulnerable pass defense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Jaguars surrender 277.2 passing yards per game, ranking 30th. Conversely, they allow an NFL-best 63.8 rushing yards per game and just 2.9 yards per carry. Houston therefore has good reason to attack through Stroud rather than repeatedly challenge Jacksonville's strongest area. Stroud has already thrown for 1,402 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions through five games. Against Tennessee, he completed 26 of 34 attempts for 261 yards, including an impressive eight completions on 11 pressured throws for 115 yards. The prediction requires Houston to convert passing volume into touchdowns, something it has not consistently accomplished. Harrison's arrival creates another possible weapon, although his debut and workload remain uncertain. This call rests primarily on Stroud's existing production and Jacksonville's passing-yardage vulnerability, not an assumption that the newcomer immediately dominates. Will Anderson Jr. records four sacks as Houston forces three turnovers Anderson delivered three of Houston's four sacks against Tennessee, providing the foundation for an even bigger prediction against Jacksonville. Four sacks by one player would be a spectacular follow-up, not merely continued improvement. The Texans limited the Titans to 187 total yards and three points after DeMeco Ryans reclaimed defensive play-calling duties. Tennessee's struggling offense makes that result an imperfect measuring stick, but Houston still ranks ninth in yards allowed per play. Jacksonville presents a tougher opponent, yet Sunday exposed pressure points. Trevor Lawrence threw an interception and lost a fumble against Philadelphia despite producing 331 passing yards and two touchdowns. Houston must turn disruptive plays into possession changes, rather than simply allowing Jacksonville to reset after sacks. The Jaguars' penalty problems could help create those opportunities. They have committed at least 13 penalties and accumulated more than 100 penalty yards in consecutive games. Backward movement makes passing situations more predictable, giving Anderson additional chances to attack. The bold call is four Anderson sacks and three Houston takeaways: pressure converts Jacksonville's mistakes into decisive field-position advantages. The Texans win by at least 17 points Jacksonville's winning record and scoring defense make a comfortable Houston victory the biggest leap here. The Jaguars have allowed only 70 points across five games, while the Texans entered last Sunday without a win. Nevertheless, a blowout becomes plausible if the first two predictions connect. Houston's passing offense attacks Jacksonville's statistical weakness, while turnovers supply short fields and prevent Lawrence from answering every score. Jacksonville also needed a 53-yard kickoff return and Cam Little's 57-yard field goal to escape Philadelphia. That extraordinary finish demonstrated resilience, but it should not conceal how close the Jaguars came to losing. Stroud's four touchdown passes power the offense, and defensive disruption keeps the Jaguars from turning their rushing balance into sustained control. London delivers a division-changing upset, not another last-second escape. The Texans are coming off their first win while the Jags take the field following their most unlikely win of the season. A preseason favorite of many to contend for the Super Bowl, Houston finally got into the win column last week with an impressive 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville. For the first time this season, the highly touted Texans dominated defensively, limiting Tennessee to just three points and 187 Total Yards. C.J. Stroud connected on passes to seven different receivers and threw for 261 yards to lead the attack on offense. Jacksonville, meanwhile, won a game they may not have deserved but were glad to have been gifted. They knocked off the Eagles, 19-17, at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Philadelphia took the lead with eight seconds remaining. Jacksonville was without a timeout, but Ameer Abdullah managed to return the ensuing kickoff 53 yards in seven seconds. Cam Little then converted a 57-yard field goal as time expired to win the game for the Jags. Jacksonville has now won three straight. The Jacksonville Jaguars have found a replacement for defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton , who served as the team's long snapper for most of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles in London. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday that the long snapper was arriving shortly, and he's now at The Grove with the rest of the team. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars will sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer , while typical starting long snapper Ross Matiscik recovers from a shoulder injury sustained in the first quarter against Philly. Who is long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer, Ross Matiscik's replacement? Bobenmoyer, 29, has spent seven years in the NFL with two teams: the Denver Broncos (2019-2022) and the Las Vegas Raiders (2023-2025). Bobenmoyer has played 97 games, recording 22 tackles and 1 fumble recovery. Jacksonville is currently overseas in London as it prepares to play its second of two matchups across the pond. The Jaguars will take on the Houston Texans in Week 6. According to Rapoport, Bobenmoyer has already flown to London. Hamilton stepped in for Jacksonville after Matiscik was injured. Teams typically carry only one long snapper on their 53-man roster or practice squad. Sunday's win marked the second time Hamilton served as the team's long snapper after Matiscik's injury. Hamilton helped set up Cam Little 's game-winning 57-yard field goal . Although Hamilton's snap was high, punter Logan Cooke got the ball down quickly, giving Little time to boot it through the uprights. The Jaguars won in the final seconds against the Eagles, 19-17. The Jaguars (4-1) will face off against the Texans in Week 6 at Wembley Stadium as they look to bury their division rival. The Texans are currently 1-4 after netting their first win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. You can follow him on X (formerly Twitter) at @Demetrius82 or on Bluesky at Demetrius .

home.blurb: And in all, four players wound up not participating, while a few others found their way onto the injury report as either a limited or full participant. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect David Montgomery, Jalen Pitre Out as Expected David Montgomery, Jalen Pitre Out as Expected Two of the non-participants from the Texans' Wednesday practice were to be expected: that's running back David Montgomery, who's dealing with a groin injury, as well as defensive back Jalen Pitre, who suffered an AC joint sprain during last weekend's game against the Tennessee Titans. As of now, their status is considered week-to-week, meaning there's a good chance that both could be sidelined for Week 6 against the Jaguars, yet might not have to be forced on injured reserve, which would take them out for a minimum of four weeks. The two other DNPs from the Texans' practice— linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair and Trent Brown— have both been dealing with some nagging injuries through the past couple of weeks that effectively left them to sit out of Wednesday's practice. However, considering both played in last week's game against the Titans while dealing with their respective injuries, it'd be fair to assume that both are still on track to play in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Henry To'oTo'o Trending Up for Return The Texans officially activated the 21-day return window for Henry To'oTo'o on Wednesday, who's been sidelined for the past four weeks due to a shoulder injury he suffered in Week 1 against the Buffalo Bills. A limited participation in practice is a great sign that his return is right around the corner. However, he might still be ruled inactive for Week 6 against the Jaguars if unable to complete a full practice. If that's the case, Jake Hansen will remain Houston's fill in as their WLB. Another aspect of the Texans' injury report that can't go unnoticed: wide receiver Tank Dell has participated in his first full practice since being designated to return from his knee injury suffered back in 2024. That means, if all goes smoothly over the coming days, there's a chance that Dell could make his long-awaited return to the lineup in Week 6. But until the Texans officially activate him from injured reserve , we won't know for sure about when he'll officially be good to be elevated on the gameday roster. home.headline: Jaguars Injury Report: Updates on Eric Murray, While Rookies Get Dinged Up
home.blurb: As for those who were limited on Sunday, the Jaguars had Tight end Nate Boerkircher (back), right tackle Cole Van Lanen (knee), rookie guard Emmanuel Pregnon (toe), cornerback Jarrian Jones (elbow), cornerback Jourdan Lewis (hamstring), cornerback Jaylon Jones (hamstring) and safety Eric Murray (concussion). Jones, Lewis, and Jaylon Jones were all limited last week, so not big updates there. Murray was also limited for most of last week's practices, though he did miss Sunday's game against the Eagles following a sustained concussion in Week 4 against the Cincinnati Bengals. The Jaguars started Rayuan Lane in his place, while former practice squad safety Kaevon Merriweather also got a big boost in playing time. Jaguars Injury Report: Updates on Eric Murray, While Rookies Get Dinged Up Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are hoping to get healthier by Sunday. The Jaguars are facing a number of injury issues before their Week 6 battle with the Houston Texans, and that was even before Wednesday's injury report was released to start the week. The Jaguars had two players miss Wednesday's practice with long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) and cornerback Montaric Brown (hamstring). The Jaguars signed new long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer to the practice squad this week to give them a chance to have a full-time option at the position after Matiscik got hurt early in last week's game against the Eagles. Brown missed Week 4 with a hamstring injury before returning last week against the Eagles. Brown played just six snaps last week , however, before leaving the game, making it clear that he is still not 100%. As things stand today, it would appear the Jaguars are on track to miss Brown when they line up against the Texans on Sunday. “Yeah, I think we'll see today and tomorrow, be able to see him run around a little bit, see what that looks like, hopeful. But he hasn't been able to do a ton since last week," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said before practice on Wednesday from the United Kingdom. "Eric just brings a calming confidence. Obviously, the communication being at a premium, it helps take some stuff off Antonio [S Antonio Johnson] as well, which I thought Antonio really stepped up last week and had one of his best games as a Jaguar in terms of just the playmaking, but also the communication and getting us right back there. It's great to have Eric. He's a competitor, he's physical, he brings a standard to everything that we do in the back end, and obviously he's playing against his former team.” On top of the Murray injury, the Jaguars also saw two rookies added to the injury report in tight end Nate Boerkircher (back) and offensive lineman Emmanuel Pregnon (toe). Boerkircher and Pregnon have each been critical to the Jaguars' success on the running game and in 12 personnel this season, with Pregnon starting all five games at left guard and Boerkircher serving as a significant addition to the rushing attack. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Sam Householder Thu, October 15, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears look to rebound from an ugly, humiliating loss to the Green Bay Packers while going on the road for the second straight week. This time, they should get starting QB Caleb Williams back. But he's going to have a fight on his hands. The Atlanta Falcons have an explosive offense with stars Drake London and Bijan Robinson. Robinson is making a case for being one of, if not the , best running back in the league. Certainly among elite company like Kenneth Walker III, Jahmyr Gibbs, Derrick Henry and James Cook. Michael Penix Jr., the quarterback taken seven spots after Williams, is a great facilitator for Kevin Stefanski's offense. He looks set to play despite a rib injury suffered late against the Ravens last week. Penix's biggest issue over his first three seasons has been availability. Sunday will be his 16th start and 18th overall game. Let's dive a little deeper into the Falcons and their history against Chicago. Atlanta Falcons SB Nation site : The Falcoholic Record: 2-3, second in the NFC South Last week: 30-23 loss in OT to the Ravens Game day, time, TV: Sunday, noon CT, FOX Spread: Bears -1.5 Bears all-time record against: 16-14 Historical meetings: The Bears and Falcons met in week 6 of the 2013 season with both teams at 2-3. The teams traded field goals, but Chicago found the end zone first with a 3-yard pass to Josh Morgan from Jay Cutler. This game ended up being a Bears-career high in passing yards for Cutler. He threw for 381 yards but just one touchdown. However, they had two 100-yard receiving games from Brandon Marshall (113) and Alshon Jeffery (136). Matt Forte rushed for two touchdowns. A late Matt Ryan interception helped seal it and the Bears won 27-13. Last meeting: Remember when there was very brief excitement that Matt Eberflus was building something? Week 17 of the 2023 season, the Bears moved to 7-9 when they stomped the Falcons 37-17 at Soldier Field. Taylor Heinicke threw three interceptions and was eventually benched for Desmond Ridder, who also threw a pick. Justin Fields threw a touchdown to DJ Moore, who had 159 yards. Fields also rushed for a touchdown, along with Khalil Herbert and Roschon Johnson. Herbert also had 124 yards. Injury report: The Falcons had three players on their Wednesday injury report. Did not participate CB C.J. Henderson (groin) Limited participation LB Divine Deablo (hamstring) DE Za'Darius Smith (concussion/neck) Offense: The Falcons offense ranks 13th in points and 10th in yards. Their rushing offense ranks second and their passing offense ranks 21st. The Falcons have gotten hot offensively since Michael Penix (67.5 pct. cmp./719 yds./3 TD/1 INT) came back. It helps to have Bijan Robinson (102 att./580 yds./4 TD), who leads the league in rushing. And Drake London (27 rec./488 yds./0 TD), who averages 18.1 yards per reception but somehow has no touchdowns. Bijan (18 rec./152 yds./1 TD) is actually their second-leading receiver. Followed by TE Kyle Pitts (10/109/1) and Jahan Dotson (8/149/1). Austin Hooper (5/40/1), Zachariah Branch (7/46/0) and former Bear Olamide Zaccheaus (4/17/0) are also role players. Behind Bijan is the other B. Robinson, Brian (51/210/4), who gets a fair share of carries inside the red zone. Defense: The Falcons defense ranks 21st in points and 16th in yards. Their rushing defense ranks fourth and their passing defense ranks 27th. S Xavier Watts (34 tkl/1 INT/2 PD/1 FF), LB Divine Deablo (16 tkls/1 PD/1 TFL/2 QB hits), CB Mike Hughes (25 tkls/1 TFL/3 PD) and CB C.J. Henderson (25 tkls/1 TFL/6 PD/1 FF) are the tackling leaders. S Jessie Bates III (24 tkls/2 PD/1 FR) and Za'Darius Smith (2.5 sk/4 TFL/3 QB hits) are two of the bigger names on the unit, but there is plenty of talent elsewhere, too. Cameron Thomas (2 sk/10 QB hits/1 TFL/1 FF) and Samson Ebukam (2.5 sk/9 QB hits/2 TFL) are among the leading pass-rushers. Gervon Dexter (0.5 sk/2 TFL/3 QB hits) is making himself comfortable in Atlanta's defensive scheme, too. Key matchups: The defense is going to have its hands full with Atlanta's playmakers. Bijan is tough for any team to contain. Combine him with London, who is a threat all over the field, and Dennis Allen's unit will have its hands full. Until last week's Ravens game, the Falcons have held opponents' rushing attack in check. It was opponents' aerial attacks that were doing damage. Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams will have to find the right balance to keep the Bears on the field, minimize Atlanta's time of possession, while scoring as many points as they can. The Bears can hang in a shootout, but Chicago will want the ball last. The Falcons' offense has turned the ball over in four of their five games. Atlanta has allowed nine passing touchdowns to three rushing touchdowns. The nine passing TD is tied for the fifth-most in the league. Opponents have the second-most pass attempts in the league against Atlanta, behind only Detroit. Atlanta has just one interception on the season, as well. The Falcons offense has the second-fewest pass attempts in the league and the second-most rushing attempts. While Chicago's red zone offensive woes are well-documented, Atlanta ranks seventh in offensive red zone scoring, getting in 69.2 percent of their trips.

The 26-year-old's return in Week 3 provided a much-needed spark to the Falcons' offense, as Atlanta scored just 16 points combined in Weeks 1 and 2 (both losses) before erupting for 80 points over the next two contests, which were victories. The Chicago Bears could get quarterback Caleb Williams back under center in Week 6 versus the Atlanta Falcons as the former No. 1 overall pick continues to recover from a hamstring injury. Atlanta head coach Kevin Stefanski gave a positive injury update Wednesday regarding the 2024 eighth overall draft pick. Penix Jr. missed the first two games of the campaign while making his way back from last season's partially-torn ACL. Penix Jr. suffered his rib injury in the fourth quarter of Sunday night's loss against the Baltimore Ravens and was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa for overtime. The latter threw a game-ending pick-six in the extra frame and the Falcons fell to the Ravens, 30-23. It was reported on Monday that Penix Jr.'s injury "is not considered serious," but Atlanta "wants to be cautious and see him practice this week" before making a decision for Week 6. The former University of Washington quarterback is 52-for-77 with 719 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception for a 104.8 passer rating across three games this fall.

away.headline: Latest injury update on Bears QB Caleb Williams in Week 6
away.blurb: Williams returned to practice last Friday, in limited fashion, and he was questionable for Week 5 vs. the Packers . But Williams was inactive for the game, which was expected, with reports indicating he was poised to return in Week 6 vs. the Falcons. Bears coach Ben Johnson announced that Caleb Williams will be a full participant on Wednesday's injury report. This will be a walkthrough practice, so the injury report is an estimate. Still, it's a great sign for Williams and his potential return this Sunday against the Falcons. Mike Garafolo says Caleb Williams 'trending in right direction' for return vs. Falcons Ian Rapoport says Caleb Williams trending towards Week 6 return According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Williams is poised for a return to the lineup this Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons. "All signs point to Caleb Williams being back on the field this week for Chicago," Rapoport said. Williams has missed the last three games with a Grade 2 hamstring injury, which tracks with the 3-4 week timetable. Williams is still considered week-to-week with his hamstring injury, but he did return to practice last Friday and participated in limited fashion. Following Week 5, head coach Ben Johnson said that Williams is """He's on track," "on track" and that he could return vs. the Falcons or after. "I think it's going to be close." There's optimism that Williams will return for Week 6 against the Falcons, but nothing is confirmed. The fact that Williams returned to practice last Friday, as a limited participant, and participated in a strenuous pre-game workout before Sunday's game against the Packers bodes well for his availability. But Thursday's injury report (Wednesday is a walkthrough) should be a good indicator of his potential return this week ahead of a short week Week 7 game against the New England Patriots. Williams suffered a Grade 2 hamstring injury in a Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, where the expectation is he would miss 3-4 weeks. Heading into Week 6, Williams has surpassed the three-week mark. We'll be keeping track of the latest updates surrounding Williams' availability for Sunday's game against the Falcons. Stay tuned. away.headline: Bears Montez Sweat suspended two games for violating NFL's PED policy
away.blurb: Although he is supposed to be one of Chicago’s top defenders, Sweat has had a poor season, with only two sacks and seven tackles through the first five games. His overall PFF grade of 55.9 so far this year is also among the lowest for edge rushers in the NFL. This was the first time Sweat was suspended in his career, though he was fined twice for horse collar tackles: once in 2020with the Washington Commanders and again in 2024 with the Bears. Sweat’s suspension was incredibly costly. Not only will he forfeit $2.3 million from the two games he is suspended for, but all future guarantees are no longer guaranteed. That includes his $12.7 million remaining for this year and $21 million next season. Given his performance and the new financial situation caused by the suspension, it wouldn't be surprising to see Chicago move on from Sweat. This likely won't happen until the end of the season, since the Bears lack depth on the defensive line right now.

away.headline: 1985 Chicago Bears to Get TV Limited Series from Steve Pink, Sunset Lane Media (Exclusive)
away.blurb: Netflix Film VP Doug Belgrad Out in Layoffs Sunset Lane Media, the banner run by executive-turned-producer David Beaubaire, has optioned Monsters: The 1985 Chicago Bears and the Wild Heart of Football , Rich Cohen’s acclaimed account of one of the most famous teams in American sports, and has assembled an offensive lineup to adapt the story as an event limited series. “This is a love letter to Chicago and to a moment when a city that had waited so long to win finally had a team that seemed unstoppable,” said Beaubaire, who is one of the exec producers of Netflix’s hit series Night Agent . “And the story wasn’t just playing out on the field. It was in the locker room, the stands, the bars and the family rooms across the city. It was riveting, funny, emotional and completely chaotic. We want to recapture that time in all its glory and chaos, remind people why we love these teams and this game so much, and show why, as cities go, Chicago is second to none.” The team went 15-1 in the season, shut out both opponents on the road to the Super Bowl, and defeated the New England Patriots 46-10 in Super Bowl XX, which was watched live by more than 92 million people, then the largest television audience in American history. 50 Cent Jokingly Takes Credit for Diddy's Head Injury, Calls Out Vivica A. away.headline: Injury Update: Bears RB Kyle Monangai ruled out, QB Caleb Williams questionable for Packers game
away.blurb: Injury Update: Bears RB Kyle Monangai ruled out, QB Caleb Williams questionable for Packers game Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Molly Kaiser/Chicago Bears Bears running back Kyle Monangai has been ruled out of Sunday's game in Green Bay with a toe injury he sustained in last weekend's 23-12 win over the Jets. "We were certainly conscious of the thumb, and it turns out the toe is a bigger deal than we initially anticipated," said coach Ben Johnson, who described Monangai's status as week-to-week. "We've got him with a specialist and so we'll work through that. He's in a boot currently and we'll go from there." Running back D'Andre Swift was a full participant in Friday's practice and was not given an injury designation for Sunday's game after sitting out Wednesday and being limited Thursday with hip and knee issues. With Monangai out, fourth-year running back Roschon Johnson moves up a spot to No. 2 on the depth chart. The 6-foot, 227-pounder has rushed for 16 yards on four carries this year—all in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's win over the Jets. "Bigger body than the other guys in that room, and so I think he's a complete back. He can run hard in between the tackles. I think he's got enough speed to get to the perimeter. He catches the ball well out of the backfield and then because of his size, I think he's an asset in pass protection as well. So, he can do a little bit of everything, which we really value at that spot." Quarterback Caleb Williams, meanwhile, returned to practice on a limited basis Friday for the first time since injuring his hamstring in the fourth quarter of a Week 2 game against the Vikings. He is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest, though Johnson announced Monday that Tyson Bagent will start in Green Bay. Johnson said that it's "highly likely" the Bears will activate one of the three players who are on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list: Cornerback Kyler Gordon, defensive lineman Shemar Turner and Noah Sewell. Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Seattle Seahawks (-2.5) at Denver Broncos (TNF) Dajani ( Seahawks -2.5): Through five weeks, I have only bet against the Denver Broncos once. It's an uncomfortable position to be in, since Bo Nix is "captain comeback." For example, I had zero doubt they would come back from down 16-0 against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3. Denver has the most comeback wins (15), second-half comebacks (12) and fourth-quarter comebacks (8) in the NFL since 2025. However, I'm going to fade the Broncos in this spot for a couple of reasons. One, Sean Payton taking back play-calling duties did not help anything against the Los Angeles Chargers . Getting this offense off the ground is, unfortunately, going to take some time -- and it probably won't happen against the No. 1 defense in the NFL. Secondly, the Seahawks have to be mad after that loss to the 49ers. Seattle has won five straight games following a loss, having not lost back-to-back games since 2024. The Seahawks have also won seven straight prime-time games, which is the longest active streak in the NFL. … Prediction: Seahawks 23, Broncos 20 Dubin (Seahawks -2.5): Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have resulted in the Broncos coming away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Patrick Surtain II here, which is obviously a problem against Jaxon Smith-Njigba . … Prediction: Seahawks 24, Broncos 16 Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was

picks.blurb: Lamar Jackson Injury: Oddsmakers Explain How They're Approaching Ravens vs. Browns Odds in NFL Week 6 Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson did not practice on Wednesday ahead of the team’s Week 6 clash against the Cleveland Browns, putting his status in question for the AFC North rivalry matchup. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson is “day-to-day” with the ankle injury that he suffered in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans. Jackson did not play in the Ravens’ win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5, as Tyler Huntley (three total scores) led Baltimore to a victory – their third straight with him in the lineup for an injured Jackson dating back to the 2025 season. Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. There has been a ton of movement in the odds for this game between the Ravens and Browns, as oddsmakers are gauging whether or not the two-time league MVP will play. Sports Illustrated spoke with several oddsmakers to give bettors some insight into how the spread for this game is currently set, and where it could move if Jackson doesn’t play. “The line this week indicates Jackson is around 60/40 to go and a revision will be made one way or the other once we know more on his status,” Johnny Avello, Director of Race and Sports Operations for DraftKings Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “There were no adjustments made with the Ravens winning on Sunday night, since backups don’t usually play as well in back-to-back games as opponents have more time to prepare.” After the Ravens opened as 3.5-point favorites against the Browns on Sunday night, that line has moved quite a bit toward Baltimore. The Ravens were 4.5-point favorites early in the week and moved as far as 5.5-point favorites at home books after ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday that Jackson had a “realistic” chance to play against Cleveland. However, the star quarterback then missed practice, causing some books to adjust the line towards the Browns. “We're sitting at five on our site,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated on Wednesday. “As it currently stands as of this moment, and as Lamar's status becomes murkier, that will likely go further towards the Browns.” Still, the opening number that books shared baked in an expectation for the two-time MVP to play. Jackson’s injury isn’t considered to be a long-term issue, and he’s been one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL when he’s been able to take the field in 2026. In his four games in the 2026 campaign, Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his passes in 2026 for 967 yards, six scores and one pick while adding 18 carries for 144 yards and a score on the ground. "Looking at this line, we are expecting Lamar to play," Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated . "It will drop to under three if Lamar ends up being out. No change for Baltimore, Snoop (Huntley) is a capable backup who has similar strengths to Lamar. They do not need to change their offense when Lamar is out, which is very helpful." While BetMGM has priced Sunday’s game with the expectation that Jackson will be in the lineup, not every book has done so. FanDuel considers Jackson “questionable” in Week 6, yet it still has the Ravens as 5.5-point favorites on Thursday. “We are pricing the Browns Ravens game as if Lamar is truly questionable to play,” a FanDuel trader told Sports Illustrated. “If he is announced in/out the line will move to or away from the Ravens based on his status. Tyler Huntley's performance last week may affect this week's matchup with the Browns, but it will not change the outlook on Baltimore as a whole as their ceiling and range of outcomes is firmly tied to Lamar Jackson's health." Thursday’s practice for Baltimore will likely impact this line, as another DNP from Jackson would be a concerning sign for his chances of playing on Sunday. The Ravens are still capable of winning games with Huntley, who has completed 78.0 percent of his passes for 264 yards and two scores in 1.5 games this season. He’s also carried the ball 10 times for 36 yards and a score. Bettors that want to take the Ravens may want to wait for a more concrete update around Jackson’s status, as it seems pretty clear the betting market has set the spread for this game with the expectation that he’s more likely to play than not. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Eagles QB Jalen Hurts out for Week 6 due to superficial blood clot TRENDING Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 2:04 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns are coming off their first loss since Week 1 as they head into Week 6. They are now 3-2 and have a pivotal matchup with the Baltimore Ravens on the horizon in what has now become a must-win game for them. The Browns can only control what they can control, and in Week 6 that is going to be more important than ever. The Ravens have been dealing with several injuries, including the most notable one regarding Lamar Jackson. Whether he plays or not, this defense needs to prepare the way they know how to. On offense, Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson have to find that spark again after losing the momentum they had been building. Without doing both of those things, this could be a major setback for the season as a whole. With that said, we have our eyes on three matchups within this game that we want to highlight. Carson Schwesinger vs. Lamar Jackson Carson Schwesinger has played at an All-Pro level this year, but he is dealing with an ankle injury. Also dealing with an ankle injury is Lamar Jackson. Neither man is likely to be 100%, so who will have the willpower to overcome the other? Schwesinger has been really flashing his pass-rush presence in 2026, which will help contain Lamar Jackson, but he also has just done a tremendous job patrolling the middle of the field. He will have to be on his A game against one of the best players of this generation. Denzel Ward vs. Zay Flowers Denzel Ward is quietly having one of the best seasons of his career, just as Zay Flowers is. The Browns cornerback has allowed an average of just 20 yards to players he is covering in 2026. On the flip side, Zay Flowers is averaging 97.3 yards per game, something has to give, right? Flowers has been pretty well contained in his career against the Browns, but every matchup is a fresh start. Whoever wins this matchup between two proverbial titans could tip the scales in their team's favor. Todd Monken vs. Jessee Minter Todd Monken will be playing against the team he left to become a head coach this offseason. He is familiar with the Ravens, Lamar Jackson, Zay Flowers, and everyone on that offense, so what will he be able to do to help Mike Rutenberg and his defense? On the flip side, Jesse Minter is looking to continue the hot start to his coaching career as the Ravens themselves are sitting pretty at 4-1. These coaches seem poised to face each other for years, but the first matchup will perhaps be the most interesting. away.headline: Ravens linked to Dolphins' former 11.5-sack edge rusher as Baltimore's pass rush stalls at 10 sacks
away.blurb: Baltimore’s sacks have been spread thin. Tavius Robinson leads the team with three, Mike Green has two, and Hendrickson had one in three games before the injury. Green had his best day in the overtime win at Atlanta, with a sack, two quarterback hits and two tackles for loss, but no Ravens rusher has more than three sacks. Head coach Jesse Minter sounded hopeful Monday that his top edge rusher could return against the Browns. Trey Hendrickson’s Potential Return Could Be Disastrous For Browns Offensive Line The Baltimore Ravens are 4-1 and atop the AFC North, but they’ve gotten there without much heat on opposing quarterbacks. With Trey Hendrickson sidelined by a finger injury the last two weeks, Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay pointed Baltimore toward a pass rusher who once had 11.5 sacks in a season: Miami Dolphins edge Josh Uche. Kay proposed sending a 2027 sixth-round pick to the winless Dolphins for Uche in his one trade for each of the NFL’s best teams . He noted that the Ravens are generating pressure on about 20.2% of plays, with a 5.52% sack rate and 10 sacks through five games. Josh Uche is playing like a starter again Uche’s best year came with the Patriots in 2022, when he had 11.5 sacks. He bounced from New England to Kansas City to Philadelphia over the next three seasons before signing a one-year deal in Miami, and he’s been productive there. PFF grades Uche 33rd of 106 edge defenders with a 71.7 overall mark, and he has 10 pressures on 111 pass-rush snaps. He also has 20 tackles, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. “I think Trey will be chomping at the bit to be ready to roll this week,” Minter said during his Monday news conference . Even with Hendrickson back, Uche would give Baltimore another rusher to rotate in. The cost is minimal. He’s on a one-year, $1.4 million deal with a $1.215 million base salary, and the Ravens have about $2.4 million in cap space, per Over the Cap . For a team that wants M&T Bank Stadium rocking in January, a sixth-round pick for a 28-year-old rusher is an easy call to make before the Nov. 10 deadline. away.headline: Major injury update for Lamar Jackson and the Ravens
away.blurb: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Jackson could be available for Sunday’s AFC North matchup against the Cleveland Browns, providing an encouraging development for a Ravens team looking to maintain its early-season momentum. “Ravens QB Lamar Jackson has a realistic chance to return for Sunday’s game at Cleveland, per league source,” Schefter reported Wednesday. The update comes after Jackson suffered an ankle injury during Baltimore’s Week 4 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Jackson exited the game at halftime and did not return, leaving backup quarterback Tyler Huntley to finish the contest. The Ravens held on for a 24-18 victory, but Jackson’s injury immediately raised concerns about how long Baltimore might be without its two-time NFL MVP. Those concerns increased when Jackson missed practice the following week and was eventually ruled out against Atlanta. However, the latest report suggests his absence could be limited to just one game. “To Lamar’s credit, he’s doing everything he can to get back out there,” Minter added. “I think we’ll know more by the middle of the week.” Jackson’s potential return would be significant for a Baltimore offense that has relied heavily on his ability to create plays through the air and on the ground. Through four appearances this season, Jackson has completed 70.8% of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception. Although the Ravens would welcome his return, Huntley has helped keep the team moving in his absence. His participation in practice and how his ankle responds throughout the week will likely play an important role in determining whether he can return against Cleveland. The Baltimore Ravens could be getting their starting quarterback back sooner than expected. After missing Baltimore’s Week 5 victory over the Atlanta Falcons with an ankle injury, Lamar Jackson reportedly has a realistic chance of returning to the field this weekend. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter had already offered an encouraging update Monday, explaining that Jackson was making progress in his recovery. “He’s definitely doing better,” Minter said . Minter also acknowledged that the team was still evaluating whether Jackson would be ready to participate in practice Wednesday. Wide receiver Chris Moore was also upgraded from limited to full with an ankle, and left tackle Ronnie Stanley has also been upgraded to a full participant. home.blurb: Jackson has a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game at Cleveland," ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Wednesday. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter later told reporters that Jackson is considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson could be back on the field in time for a Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported the Ravens are "hopeful" Trey Hendrickson—who has missed two games with a thumb injury—returns this week. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. home.headline: Ravens receive big Lamar Jackson injury update ahead of Week 6 game vs Browns
home.blurb: Lamar Jackson could return from his ankle injury against the Browns in Week 6, giving the Ravens a crucial boost in the tight AFC North race. The Baltimore Ravens could receive a major boost for their Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns, as quarterback Lamar Jackson could return from an ankle injury. Jackson missed Sunday’s game against the Atlanta Falcons, but the latest report from ESPN insider Adam Schefter offers reason for optimism as Baltimore prepares for a crucial AFC North showdown. Schefter shared the update on Wednesday, indicating that Jackson could be back on the field this weekend. The ESPN insider reported: “Ravens QB Lamar Jackson has a realistic chance to return for Sunday’s game at Cleveland, per league source.” Although the report does not guarantee Lamar will play, it suggests the former MVP could avoid an extended absence. The star QB suffered the ankle injury during Baltimore’s Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans and was unable to play against Atlanta. The Ravens nevertheless found a way to secure a dramatic overtime victory against the Falcons, showing they could remain competitive without their franchise quarterback. However, with the AFC North race tightening, having Jackson available against Cleveland could prove crucial to Baltimore’s hopes of maintaining its position in the division. For now, Baltimore has not officially confirmed who will start at quarterback against Cleveland. Jackson’s availability will depend on how his ankle responds during the week and whether he can return to practice. Head coach Jesse Minter previously said Jackson was improving, but the team was still evaluating his progress before making a decision. If Jackson is cleared to play, the Ravens would regain their most dynamic offensive weapon for a matchup with significant divisional implications. His dual-threat ability as a passer and runner changes the way opposing defenses must prepare, giving Baltimore more options in an offense built around his unique skill set. His return would also provide a significant lift after the team had to rely on its backup in Atlanta. If Jackson cannot play, Tyler Huntley is expected to start for the second consecutive game. Huntley helped Baltimore earn the overtime win against the Falcons and would once again be tasked with leading the offense if Jackson remains sidelined. The Ravens will continue monitoring their quarterback’s recovery throughout the week, with his practice participation likely to offer the clearest indication of whether he will return against the Browns. It's a welcomed return home after a road trip that produced mixed results. After traveling to London and collecting a win, things went sideways in Pittsburgh. FanDuel Sportsbook is giving the Colts the edge against the winless Titans with a 6.5-point spread advantage. The money line is at -330 with the over/under starting at 43.5. The Colts did what they do; they lost in Pittsburgh. Unable to finish drives and giving up huge plays on defense was the story of the afternoon. After going up 3-0, they never regained the lead. Every time the Colts got close, they had to settle for 3. Luckily, Spencer Schrader was on his game, but it wasn't enough. An 80 and 50 yard score by Jaylen Warren was too much to overcome as the Colts fell, once again, to the Steelers in Pittsburgh. The Titans and Texans were entrenched in the battle of the winless as one team would get off the schneid and the other would sink further down. Cam Ward and the Titans might really be that bad. Lose again and the Titans might be eyeing a replacement for Ward in the draft with the No. 1 pick. The Colts have work to do, but the Titans might be the best remedy to what ails them. Nothing is certain, but this is a great opportunity to get to 3-3 and finish the first third of the season at .500. Finding the end zone and putting up 6 in place of 3 is a great place to start. Offensive lineman Matt Goncalves and rookie defensive end Jaylahn Tuimoloau were both limited Wednesday after leaving practice to undergo concussion evaluations. Outside of Josh Downs, there just haven't been many sparks from this group. Downs leads the healthy receivers with 20 catches for 249 yards, but he appeared on Wednesday's report as limited with rest/hamstring listed. Keenan Allen did not practice due to rest, while Ashton Dulin remained sidelined with a hamstring injury. One encouraging development was Darius Slayton returning as a full participant after a knee injury kept him out against Pittsburgh. Jonathan Taylor was limited strictly for rest, while Charvarius Ward also received a rest day. Tight end Will Mallory was another full participant as he continues working toward a potential return from injured reserve. Colts Open Week 6 With Several Key Names on Injury Report Skip to main content SI.COM At this point, Indianapolis Colts fans are probably tired of watching injuries take a toll on this roster. It feels like the same story we've seen over the last decade-plus, and through five weeks of the 2026 season, injuries are once again making life considerably more difficult for Indianapolis. Wednesday's injury report featured several notable names, including two players who left practice for concussion evaluations. And for a team sitting at 2-3, the last thing Indianapolis needs is more injuries to important contributors. Two Important Colts Undergo Concussion Evaluations Whether either player passed those evaluations remains unclear, but both situations deserve attention heading into Sunday. Goncalves has been a valuable piece of the offensive line, and with Daniel Jones already struggling to find consistency, losing another contributor up front certainly wouldn't help. Tuimoloau's situation might be even more frustrating considering the current state of Indianapolis' defensive line. With Arden Key recently landing on injured reserve, Indianapolis needs its younger pass rushers to step up and produce . Potentially losing another body along the defensive front would only make that challenge more difficult. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies also missed practice with the rib injury that sidelined him against Pittsburgh. Considering how poorly this linebacker room has performed through five weeks, Indianapolis can hardly afford another week without one of its starters.
