home.headline: Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts
home.blurb: The Colts are seeking consistency at linebacker, with snaps divided in Week 5 between Akeem Davis-Gaither (52 snaps), Austin Ajiake (32 snaps), CJ Allen (24 snaps) and Bryce Boettcher (11 snaps) with starting WILL linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) out. As with Davis-Gaither, the Colts see value in Pratt's experience not only in the NFL, but with Anarumo's system. Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts signed the 30-year-old Pratt, who started 12 games for them in 2025, to their practice squad on Tuesday. While Germaine Pratt went unsigned up until Tuesday, he found a way to still be involved in football. The 30-year-old veteran linebacker spent time in the summer as a volunteer coach at North Carolina State , where he worked with his alma mater's linebackers. He eventually had a tryout with the Dallas Cowboys, though he didn't sign. This week, Pratt got his chance to get back into playing instead of coaching. The Colts signed him to their practice squad on Tuesday, and while it's too early to tell if and when he'll make his 2026 debut, Pratt said his goal is to use his experience to bring leadership to the Colts' linebacker room. "Helping the defense, just being in this system for so long, that's all I know," Pratt said. "So help it stabilize and settle it down, make tackles, whatever the case may be, get some turnovers." Pratt has played all but four of his 112 NFL games for Lou Anarumo, his defensive coordinator with the Cincinnati Bengals (2019-2024) and Colts (2025). In 2025, Pratt signed with the Colts in October after being released by the Las Vegas Raiders and started 12 games, totaling 101 tackles, a forced fumble and an interception. The experienced WILL linebacker has had over 100 tackles with at least one interception and one forced fumble every year since 2023. "Just adding a veteran presence is big in there," head coach Shane Steichen said. "He's played a lot of football in this league, made a lot of plays, and any time you can add good players to your roster, you want to do that." In the immediate future, whether Pratt could factor into that group on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans – he'd have to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad – remains to be seen given he didn't participate in training camp and took the field for his first practice of the 2026 season on Wednesday. "I don't know the plan," Pratt said. home.blurb: Colts sign TE Pharaoh Brown to 53-man roster from practice squad, sign LB Germaine Pratt to practice squad Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts made the roster move on Tuesday. The Indianapolis Colts today signed tight end Pharaoh Brown to the 53-man roster from the practice squad. The team also signed linebacker Germaine Pratt to the practice squad. Brown , 6-5, 246 pounds, has spent the entire season on the team's practice squad. He has played in 94 career games (56 starts) in his time with the Colts (2026, 2023), Arizona Cardinals (2025), Miami Dolphins (2025), Seattle Seahawks (2024), New England Patriots (2023), Cleveland Browns (2018-20, 2022), Houston Texans (2020-22) and Oakland Raiders (2017-18). Brown has compiled 74 receptions for 752 yards (10.2 avg.) and three touchdowns. Pratt , 6-3, 250 pounds, re-joins Indianapolis after spending time with the team last season. He has started 104-of-112 career games in his time with the Colts (2025), Las Vegas Raiders (2025) and Cincinnati Bengals (2019-24) and has totaled 734 tackles (416 solo), 38.0 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, 33 passes defensed, eight interceptions, eight forced fumbles, seven fumble recoveries and eight special teams stops. Pratt has started seven postseason contests and has compiled 49 tackles (32 solo), 1.0 tackle for loss, four passes defensed and one interception. In 2025, he started 12 games with Indianapolis and registered 101 tackles (57 solo), 5.0 tackles for loss, eight passes defensed, one interception, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries. The Dallas Cowboys entered Thursday night’s showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as 9.5-point favorites, yet they lost outright at home, destroying plenty of Survivor entries in the process. Week 5 had three teams that were obvious Survivor selections: Dallas, Houston and Cincinnati. They were all playing 0-4 teams, but only the Bengals and Texans came through. Luckily for the SI Betting team, neither of our editors selected the Cowboys this week, meaning that if you tailed our picks , you’re still alive heading into Week 6. Bye weeks are really starting to come into play in Survivor, as the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins and Bengals all won’t play in Week 6. One of the best strategies in Survivor this season has been fading the 0-5 Dolphins, so players will have to look elsewhere on Sunday. There are still some huge favorites in Week 6, the Los Angeles Rams are favored by double digits at home against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Kansas City Chiefs, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots are all favored by at least a touchdown at home. Each week, the SI Betting team of Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey makes their favorite Survivor selections each week to help guide our readers through the season. Here’s a recap of our Week 5 selections before we dive into our favorite Survivor teams in Week 6. NFL Week 5 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Houston Texans (W) Both Dewey and MacMillan faded winless teams in Week 5, and both wins were relatively sweat free with the Texans blowing out Tennessee and Cincy cruising to a big lead in a seven-point win over Miami. There are still plenty of playoff contenders that we can choose from in Week 6, even in just a 14-game slate. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 6 Survivor Pool Picks Indianapolis Colts Indianapolis is going to be a popular pick in Survivor this week because it’s playing the Titans, but I’m willing to take a shot on Daniel Jones and company to get back to .500 at 3-3, especially at home. Indy is currently a seven-point favorite against the worst team in the AFC South. Cam Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start. They’ve scored 20 or fewer points in every game, including three games where they scored 10 or less points. Indianapolis hasn’t done a great job of finishing drives this season, but it has one of the best kickers in the NFL in Spencer Shrader. So, Indy is able to get enough points on the board (like it did in Week 5) even if it doesn’t score a bunch of touchdowns. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, which is a concern for them when it comes to this pick. However, Tennessee is 2-8 on the road in the Ward era, and it has covered the spread in just four of those games. The Indy offense isn’t a juggernaut, but it has moved the ball a lot better than the Titans, hanging 30 points on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2 while ranking 21st in success rate and 22nd in EPA/Play. I don’t see many spots where I’d willingly take the Colts in Survivor, so this is a way to use them and hopefully advance to Week 7. With more bye weeks ahead, it’s important to save a few top teams – if possible – for a game that may not be as much of a sure thing. Indy at home against the Titans is by far the most favorable game on the team’s schedule outside of a Nov. 15 home game against Miami. The Titans have been lost to open this season, and I don’t expect them to turn things around any time soon with how abysmal their offense has looked. The Colts may not cover, but they should handle business at home in Week 6. – Peter Dewey New England Patriots The New England Patriots proved last week that they still can show flashes of the team that won the AFC last season, especially when they play the weaker teams in the NFL. Their defense is a top 10 unit and Drake Maye can still torch a below average secondary. The Patriots now rank 10th in EPA per play, while the New York Jets rank 20th. New England is also 11th in opponent success rate, while New York is 23rd. That could all lead to big things for the Patriots in this divisional game. The Patriots have a ton of tough games on their schedule this season, including the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, so taking them when they're at home against either the Jets or Dolphins is going to be the move, which is why this is the week I'll take them at Gillette Stadium against Geno Smith and Aaron Glenn. Plus, New England is 18-2 at home in its last 20 games against the Jets. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Drake Maye and the offense are finding their footing, and the Jets arrive after winning a game against the Browns that nobody needs to watch twice. New England's backfield takes a hit with TreVeyon Henderson expected to miss multiple weeks. More work for Rhamondre Stevenson, and another reason Maye needs to keep this passing game moving. Breece Hall's availability matters for New York. The Jets need sustained possessions, manageable third downs and a game that doesn't force them to chase points. I like the Patriots to control this one without needing another 45-point afternoon. Win the turnover battle and the rest should follow. That's a difficult blow for the Jets, who probably needed to face the more error-prone version of the quarterback in order to score an upset. Rookie David Bailey and the pass rush might give Gang Green a chance if they can keep Maye under pressure, but the defense's struggles to generate any takeaways cap the potential for chaos here. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Patriots 28, Jets 21 Everyone believes the Patriots are back. Are they? New England took advantage of a porous Bills defense and then an upstart Raiders bunch that had to travel across the country following a deflating defeat to the rival Chiefs. Credit the Patriots for taking care of business, but Drake Maye still has a long way to go before entering the circle of trust again. The Jets could get some reinforcements back this week and Aaron Glenn's defense has been respectable. The Patriots still get the job done, but it could be closer than some might expect. After losing two of their first three games, the Patriots have won their last two and appear to have righted things. They enter the week in second place in the division. The Jets also got in the win column this past weekend and are looking to build on the momentum gained in that victory. The Jets’ win was a gritty 17-12 victory over the Cleveland Browns. It was a much-needed result after three straight losses to Chicago, Detroit, and Green Bay. Geno Smith threw for 182 yards and Braelon Allen rushed for 116 as the Jets rallied late in the fourth and then held on late to secure their second win of the season. New York’s defense sacked Deshaun Watson eight times and pressured him consistently throughout the game. Rookie David Bailey dominated much of the afternoon securing three sacks in the process. After upsetting the Bills in Week 4 in Buffalo, the Patriots dismantled the Raiders 45-17 at home last weekend. back-to-back wins over Buffalo and Las Vegas. After a dreadful start to the season, Drake Maye has been special the last two weeks completing 68% of his passes and throwing for 643 yards including seven touchdowns and one interception. He has also rushed for 79 yards on 15 carries in those games. Mike Vrabel’s defense has been better than good allowing just 18.8 points per game. Among the biggest storylines Sunday are whether the Jets’ pass rush can get to Maye and pressure him, whether Smith can generate any explosive plays against a Patriots’ defense that does not allow many of them, and whether New England or the Jets will own second place in the AFC East by the end of the night. The series history favors the Patriots. Their most recent matchup came on December 28, 2025, when New England dominated the Jets 42-10. picks.headline: NY Jets vs Patriots expert picks and predictions for Week 6 game
picks.blurb: Englewood counselor accused of sexually assaulting 10-year-old boy News Bergen Sports HS Sports Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals JETS NY Jets vs Patriots expert picks and predictions for Week 6 game Albert Bainbridge IV Art Stapleton Bob Jordan Mike Dougherty Chris Iseman Brian Marron Dave Rivera NorthJersey.com Oct. 14, 2026, 6:03 a.m. ET After their worst performance of the young NFL season in Week 4, it was a complete 180 by the New York Jets in Week 5. Their defense was relentless all day as No. 2 overall pick David Bailey had a career day with three sacks in the Jets' 17-12 win over the Cleveland Browns at MetLife Stadium last Sunday. Jets RB Braelon Allen − who has started for injured star running back Breece Hall the last two games − scored the game-winning touchdown with three minutes left in regulation. The victory snapped a three-game losing streak for the Jets after opening the season with a road victory over the Tennessee Titans . It'll be tough for the Jets to replicate their performance in Week 6, as they head on the road to take on the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium, a house of horrors for Gang Green over the past 15 years. The Jets have lost 14 of their last 15 games in New England, with the lone exception being a 17-3 win during the final week of the 2023 season on Jan. 7, 2024. Our NFL prognosticators are: Art Stapleton ( Giants /NFL writer, NorthJersey.com), Bert Bainbridge (sports trending reporter/columnist, NorthJersey.com), Brian Marron (digital producer, NorthJersey.com), Chris Iseman (Rutgers writer, NorthJersey.com), Mike Dougherty (sports writer, lohud.com), Bob Jordan (sports editor, Asbury Park Press/APP.com) and Dave Rivera (sports editor, USA TODAY Northeast/NorthJersey.com). Jets vs Patriots Week 6 staff predictions, staff standings Brian Marron: 5-0 Dave Rivera: 5-0 Art Stapleton: 4-1 Bert Bainbridge: 4-1 Bob Jordan: 4-1 Mike Dougherty: 4-1 Chris Iseman : 3-2 Will the Jets pull off the upset in Foxborough? Here are our staff predictions for this AFC East battle on Sunday: Bert Bainbridge The pick: Patriots 31, Jets 13 Here's why: The Jets defense stepped up to the challenge in Week 5, but they'll face a much more difficult test on the road against a Patriots offense that's heating up after a slow start to the season. New England puts this divisional contest out of reach in the second half. Art Stapleton The pick: Patriots 27, Jets 17 Here's why: The Jets are catching the Patriots at the wrong time. Two weeks ago, Drake Maye was lost and the league was talking about his struggles. Now, after wins over the Bills and the Raiders , Maye is lighting it up. He's a different quarterback than Deshaun Watson, so don't expect Aaron Glenn's defense to have similar success. The pick: Patriots 40, Jets 17 Here's why: When the Patriots struggled to a 1-2 start, it looked like this could be a game where the Jets could extract more payback for that recent 15-game losing streak in this series. Oh well. The pick: Patriots 27, Jets 16 Here's why: The Jets are facing Drake Maye and the Patriots at the wrong time as New England is starting to get on a roll. It won't be a blowout, but the Patriots will play from ahead throughout the game. Mike Dougherty The pick: Patriots 30, Jets 17 Here's why: Drake Maye is no longer playing like a lost soul. He threw four TD passes last week against the Raiders and regained the complete trust of a sneaky good offensive group. The Jets simply don't have enough playmakers on that side of the ball to keep up. The pick: Patriots 27, Jets 13 Here's why: If not for a drop from the Browns' punter and some putrid play from Deshaun Watson, the Jets very likely enter this game on a four-game losing skid. Drake Maye and the resurgent Patriots will not provide the Jets with the same gifts. The pick: Patriots 34, Jets 13 Here's why: No way the Jets are winning two games in a row. away.blurb: The loss doesn't seem to be just in the standings for the Browns now, as reports come out of it that they saw both running back Quinshon Judkins and linebacker Carson Schqesinger leave in walking boots. Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot was the one to share this information after the game. On Monday, we didn't have an update on Judkins, but NFL Media's Ian Rapoport shared one on Schwesinger. He posted on social media, saying, "Browns star LB Carson Schwesinger suffered a Grade 1 ankle sprain in their loss against the Jets, though the injury occurred before his strip sack of Geno Smith, sources say. He is not ruled out for this week, though availability depends on how he responds." The idea of the Browns' defense losing Schwesinger for any amount of time would be devastating. The team has the Baltimore Ravens next up on the schedule, who are dealing with injuries of their own, but they need him for them and more.

away.blurb: But now, with both players banged up and out for Sunday's game, the Browns will have to dive into its depth with hopes of replacing such productivity. Browns vs Jets Week 5 Injury Report: Cleveland Without 2 Key Pieces Defensively Skip to main content SI.COM The Cleveland Browns have started the 2026 NFL regular season 3-1. And while it seems like nothing can slow this team down, the recent injury report casts such a sentiment in doubt. On Sunday, Oct. 11, the Browns are slated to take on the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J., for what should be a fairly competitive contest. The Browns and Jets aren't the league's most prominent teams, especially with how young and raw they are, but they both have boom-or-bust potential. Ahead of the showdown, the inactive list was announced , with Browns defensive linemen Mike Hall Jr. and Mason Graham stealing the spotlight. #Browns inactives v #Jets : QB Taylen Green (3QB) WR Tylan Wallace TE Carsen Ryan DT Mike Hall Jr. C Parker Brailsford G Teven Jenkins DT Mason Graham Both have been standouts on the line for the Browns this season, combining for 19 tackles, seven for a loss, six quarterback hits and five sacks. While many of those numbers skew in Graham's direction, his injury in last week's Thursday Night Football showdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers pushed Hall Jr. into a bigger role. Fortunately, he did not disappoint. On the line, the Browns are expected to deploy Maliek Collins, Adin Huntington, Chris Williams and Sam Kamara. Both Williams and Kamara were activated from the practice squad earlier in the week to fill Graham and Hall's voids. "It's next man up. I think that's really what it is," head coach Todd Monken said earlier in the week when asked about the Browns' injuries. "That's why you have practice squad players and the ability to elevate them. It's going to take everybody on the roster, and that's why you're consistently trying to develop those players. "So, when they get their number called, the expectation, the position, you're trying not to let that drop." Outside of the defensive line, the Browns also are working through injuries on the offensive side of the ball. New England Patriots starting left tackle Will Campbell suffered a knee injury during this past Sunday's Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Campbell underwent MRI testing to determine the severity of his injury on Monday. And according to a report from NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the 22-year-old offensive lineman avoided a serious, long-term injury. Campbell is now considered "week-to-week" as the Patriots prepare for this coming Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the division-rival New York Jets. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said of Campbell's injury status on Monday. “It’ll get looked at and continues to rehab. Wasn’t able to finish the game, so I don’t know how much time he’ll miss — if he’ll be back towards the end of the week, if he’ll be back Wednesday. We’ll take it day by day and see how he feels tomorrow, see what he does Wednesday, and keep you updated on the injury report.” After a slow start to the 2026 season, the Patriots are beginning to catch their stride. Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders marked the team's second consecutive victory and third win of the season thus far. Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Jets will kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

home.headline: Patriots week 6 injury report: AJ Brown returns, OTs banged up bad
home.blurb: "I mean, I think that we'll just focus on this week and see if guys are ready to go," Mike Vrabel said Wednesday about handling injuries ahead of this week and next week's Thursday Night Football game. "We obviously know we have a shortened week next week. It can’t impact our decisions to try to do everything we can to win this week. Then we’ll figure out where we are after that." The biggest story for the Patriots? The return of A.J. Brown, who missed Weeks 2 through 5 with a high-ankle sprain . He was designated to return off of IR this week, and will work to try and play this week against a Jets team he should thrive against. "He hasn't been out there, so I can't tell you until we actually see it," Vrabel said. "He hasn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him back out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple days. And if not, then we have a 21-day window, and we'll go from there." Last week against the Raiders, the Patriots lost both TreVeyon Henderson and Will Campbell in a matter of minutes. Both players would leave the game and wouldn't return, and after tests on Monday, could end up missing some time . When reporters were present during Wednesday's practice, neither of them were spotted on the field with their teammates. Campbell did speak prior to going out to practice, but he only participated in a limited capacity. When Campbell was ruled out, the Patriots turned to first round rookie Caleb Lomu . He would play pretty good football from the left side — allowing just one pressure in 47 snaps. FOXBORO — The New England Patriots have gone through a lot of injuries these last five weeks. They've been forced to put more players on injured reserve at this point in the season (19) than they did all of last season. They've been banged up , but have still won two-straight games to improve to 3-2. But they're getting some players back this week ahead of their matchup with the New York Jets. The Patriots will have three weeks to officially decide if they'll remove him off of IR and stick him on the 53-man roster. Brown participated in practice , going through drills with his receivers coach, Todd Downing. There didn't seem to be any limitations in how he looked (at least when reporters were present). The Patriots also started the 21-day window for second-year offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, who was placed on IR ahead of the regular season with an ankle injury. picks.blurb: Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Eagles QB Jalen Hurts out for Week 6 due to superficial blood clot TRENDING Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Lorenzo Styles Jr. #36 of the New Orleans Saints plays against the Minnesota Vikings during the first half of a game at Caesars Superdome on October 11, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Caleb Yaccarino Wed, October 14, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads I want to start this week's report by talking about this class. Like many, I have seen it ranked very low on lists of the best and worst classes from 2026. I don't disagree with those lists, and really, who can? Injuries, players being behind veterans, or some still needing to develop have kept this class from doing much, but you shouldn't lose faith in this group. The players who have been in the game have made plays that are good starting points, and although development matters, it's not like those players have been bad. Jordyn Tyson's injury is annoying to say the least, but hopefully we can forget about that once he's back. Do I think this class is going to be like 2025? No, but in hindsight, I think he could be a nice, middle-of-the-road draft class. Now onto the players: DT Christen Miller Finally, Christen Miller was able to get into the game on Sunday, and eventhough the Saints could not win, he did well in his short time. Miller made big plays against the run, took up blocks from offensive linemen to open up holes for other defensive linemen and the linebackers to stop the run, and in my opinion, proved he should be the starting nose tackle. It wasn't perfect, but it was enough for the Saints to play him more. This should hopefully be the case against the New York Giants, and to stop RB Cam Skattebo, you need a big defensive lineman that can prevent him from carrying the pile. TE Oscar Delp With the Vikings sending blitzes nearly every play, Delp had to step up as a blocker, and he did. The Giants are also at the top of the league in blitz rate, so Delp will be a primary blocker once again. I do hope the Saints utilize him as a receiver, because Noah Fant has had pre-snap issues this season, and prioritizing youth should be the plan moving forward. Try something new. OG Jeremiah Wright Speaking of trying something new, I wish Jeremiah Wright would get some snaps, but now that pressure is on the organization to win, a Cesar Ruiz trade feels less likely due to the risk. If a coaching change is made, I hope the next staff will give Wright a chance. WR Bryce Lance Last week, I said that it's clear Lance is not ready for WR3, and the Vikings game only reinforced that. The Saints need to make the move and put him at WR4 moving forward so he can learn. I know I have said to prioritize youth, but I also want to prioritize Tyler Shough's development, and Lance is negatively affecting that. WR Barion Brown Brown is a similar spot to Lance, but it's also clear he needs to figure out the return game as well. His fellow former LSU Tiger, Zavion Thomas, is in nearly the exact same spot with the Bears, but due to their offensive struggles with Caleb Williams being out, they have begun to utilize Thomas more. In addition, Thomas has improved as their main return man. Hopefully, the same can happen for Brown. RB CJ Donaldson Donaldson was thrown to the wolves trying to block the Vikings blitz, and although I felt he did a decent job, he did have a holding call on one of the plays. As a rusher, Donaldson did exactly what I thought, picking up tough yards that did help the Saints in their run game. Against the Giants, I want him to be included once again. OT Mason Murphy In probably the most confusing moment of the game, which is saying a lot, the Saints put in Mason Murphy on a random drive, then subbed him out for Asim Richards the next. At first, I thought Richards got injured, but Moore said after the game that it was planned. I actually thought Richards did better than usual, and Murphy wasn't great when he came in. I don't think the Saints will make this substitution again. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles Jr. was back last game, which was nice to see, but his involvement was limited. I wouldn't be shocked if that changes after Jayden Price's release being cut, so Styles Jr. could be the return man next to Brown against the Giants. Injured players: WR Jordyn Tyson

I love a good narrative, and you know there's going to be something worth watching here. The Giants keep giving themselves chances, and Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely should find room against a Saints defense that hasn't offered much resistance lately. New Orleans has dropped three straight, but New York's defense gives Tyler Shough a reasonable opportunity to bounce back from a dreadful showing versus Minnesota. Say what you want about Jameis Winston, but he's slinging it for the G-Men and keeping his team afloat. away.headline: Saints WR Chris Olave appears on injury report with new issue
away.blurb: Olave took the field for practice in a limited capacity on Thursday, but a new “foot” designation was added to the report. While this “foot” designation could be cause for concern, the fact that Olave took the field for a limited practice is a positive sign for his Week 5 status. New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave did not participate in Wednesday’s Week 5 practice session, landing on the injury report with a “rest” designation. This new issue comes as a surprise to fans and reporters who saw Olave take a hit to the knee late in Monday night’s matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. Trailing 45-17 with just over one minute remaining in the primetime contest, the superstar wide receiver limped off the field with what was assumed to be a knee injury. Olave ranks second in NFL receiving yards so far this season with 491, trailing only Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb (498). He recorded his third 100+ receiving yard game of the year in Monday’s loss to the Falcons, reeling in eight receptions for 116 yards. The 1-3 Saints will welcome the Minnesota Vikings for a Week 5 matchup this coming Sunday. away.headline: Vikings-Saints Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, some intrigue with a number of players listed as questionable, including Jordan Addison, Justin Jefferson, and Brian O’Neill. I’m gonna go out on a limb and say that all three will play on Sunday. I know they will be cautious with all of them, but it doesn’t sound like Jefferson has experienced any problems with his ankle all week. It sounds like Addison and O’Neill’s injuries are more of the minor variety they will play through. It’s not a surprise at this point that Christian Darrisaw is out, as he hadn’t practiced all week. He should be ready to go after the bye week. For the Saints, Alvin Kamara is questionable but my guess is he’ll play on Sunday. Safety Julian Blackmon is also questionable but probably will play as well. Those are the two key players on the Saints list this week. Everyone else is either listed as out or do not have a deisignation and/or are a backup. Who will be sitting this one out? away.headline: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve
away.blurb: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Eagles QB Jalen Hurts out for Week 6 due to superficial blood clot Caleb's return won't solve it all New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve Welcome back, Zach Wood. The New Orleans Saints long snapper was a full participant at practice on Wednesday, marking his return from injured reserve. He'll need to continue practicing throughout the week in order to be activated for Sunday's game with the New York Giants , but all signs point to him snapping the ball at MetLife Stadium. The Saints released fill-in long snapper Cal Adomitis and don't have another player at the position on their roster. They also left a vacancy open and waiting for Wood on the 53-man roster once he gets the green light. Wood, 33, won the job back in 2017 and was the long snapper for New Orleans in 150 consecutive regular season games (plus seven playoff games), finally ending his streak when a calf strain forced him out of action the last four weeks. The fear was that he would have needed even more time to recover, but he's ahead of schedule and expected to be back in the lineup. Wood has made quite a career for himself as a former rookie free agent out of SMU. He actually spent some time with the Dallas Cowboys when Kellen Moore was the backup quarterback in 2016 and part of the 2017 preseason. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve TRENDING Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead John Sigler, Saints Wire Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:56 AM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads He's been missed. Adomitis had some hiccups and drew an untimely penalty during Week 5's loss to the Minnesota Vikings , so getting Wood back on the field should help steady the operation. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Live Simms Unbuttoned Rotoworld Bet Staff , Rotoworld Bet Staff Fresh off their bye week, the Carolina Panthers (2-2) head to Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday looking to continue their early-season momentum as they take on the Philadelphia Eagles (2-3). Carolina enters Week 6 in first place in the NFC South, one half game ahead of the Falcons (2-3). The Panthers boast one of the league’s most productive offenses, averaging just over 30 points per game behind a breakout season from quarterback Bryce Young . Losers of three in a row, a banged-up Philadelphia is reeling a bit following a brutal loss in London this past weekend, 19-17 to Jacksonville. Prior to their bye, the Panthers outlasted the Bears in Charlotte, 32-26. The aforementioned Young threw for 329 yards and a couple touchdowns, Tetairoa McMillan caught 14 balls for 192 yards including both Young touchdown passes and Chuba Hubbard ran for 122 yards and two scores in the win. Bryce Young has now thrown for 1268 yards including nine touchdowns and just two interceptions through four games this season. Philadelphia’s most recent outing was a head-scratcher. With a patchwork offensive line and numerous skill position players sidelined, the Eagles somehow managed to take a lead over Jacksonville in London, 17-16 with eight seconds to play in the fourth quarter. The Eagles elected not to kick off through the endzone…as well as tackle kick returner Ameer Abdullah until he had rambled 53 yards to the Philly 39-yard line with one second to play. Cam Little then came on to drill a game-winning 57-yard field goal as the Eagles snatched defeat from the jaws of victory. Prior to the mayhem in the final moments, Jalen Hurts threw for 220 yards and a touchdown to Darius Cooper . Minus the injured Saquon Barkley , the Eagles rushed for a paltry 22 yards in the game. While Philadelphia’s long list of injuries tops this game’s storylines, the play under center for each team will be noteworthy. Bryce Young appears to be taking a major step forward in his third NFL season as the Panthers’ offense is currently one of the league’s most explosive. Jalen Hurts has been either really good this season (two games) or subpar (three games). It is no coincidence that the poor performances have coincided with the Birds’ three-game losing streak. A third storyline to pay attention to is the turnover battle. Carolina enters the week with a +3 turnover differential while Philadelphia has coughed the ball up two more times than it has taken the ball away. The Eagles have dominated this series winning 11 of the 13 all-time meetings including each of the last five. Their most recent meeting came on December 8, 2024, when Philadelphia escaped with a 22-16 victory. In the past, Sunday would be a get right spot for Philly, but Carolina takes the field with a substantial rest advantage and playing better football. There is something to be said however, about a desperate football team and the Eagles should be desperate come the weekend. away.blurb: Jalen Hurts Ruled Out for Week 6 vs. Panthers Due to Superficial Blood Clot | Sports Injury Central Home Features News SIC Premium Expert Picks Promotions Login Sign Up Jalen Hurts Ruled Out for Week 6 vs. Panthers Due to Superficial Blood Clot Published on October 15, 2026 at 5:12 PM | Updated October 15, 2026 at 5:13 PM Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers after a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in a superficial blood clot in his calf. However, Wednesday night's follow-up ultrasound showed movement in the clot, prompting the Eagles to rule him out while determining the appropriate treatment. "Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment," the Eagles said. "His health and safety are our highest priority." The Eagles have not announced a treatment plan or timetable for Hurts' return. Running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith have both missed time with hamstring injuries and did not practice Wednesday ahead of Week 6. NFL Deebo Samuel Ruled Out With Left Hamstring Injury After Third-Quarter Fumble Against Seahawks According to an official statement from the Eagles, Hurts initially injured his calf when he was cleated during Philadelphia's October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. Hurts first sought treatment Thursday, October 8, after practicing Wednesday and Thursday fully. He received additional treatment Friday and was added to the injury report despite another full practice. An ultrasound performed Saturday after the team arrived in London revealed a superficial blood clot. After reviewing the results, team doctors determined that Hurts could safely play, with activity and mobility considered important. Hurts played without limitations Sunday and received treatment Monday and Tuesday before practicing fully on Wednesday. His availability beyond Week 6 remains uncertain pending further medical evaluation. Tanner McKee to Start Amid Eagles Offensive Injuries Tanner McKee will start against the Panthers in Hurts' absence, taking over an Eagles offense already dealing with several significant injuries. Philadelphia's offensive line has also undergone major changes. Lane Johnson retired, Cam Jurgens was traded to Baltimore and Landon Dickerson has been on injured reserve with a knee injury. Dickerson returned to practice Wednesday after the Eagles opened his 21-day practice window. The injuries and personnel changes leave McKee facing additional challenges as he prepares to lead Philadelphia's offense against Carolina. away.blurb: Quarterback Jalen Hurts is the latest player to go down, as he's been diagnosed with a superficial blood clot and will not play in Week 6 against the Carolina Panthers. Hurts apparently played with the clot in his calf on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but the team decided to rule him out for this week after an ultra sound revaled movement in the clot. Losing Hurts has impacted the Eagles' odds for Week 6 against the Panthers, as they are now home underdogs of more than a field goal. The Eagles opened as 1.5-point favorites at home in this game, even with Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and others dealing with injuries. However, Hurts' absence caused this line to flip completely, as the Panthers are now 3.5-point favorites on the road in the odds at DraftKings . Tanner McKee is in line to start for the Eagles in Week 6, and that's a clear downgrade to the team's offense. The dual-threat quarterback hasn't been at his best this season, but he gives Philly's offense a different dimension in the ground game that McKee can't really replicate. away.headline: NFL analyst picks Panthers over Eagles for Week 6 matchup
away.blurb: Besides being out of running backs, the other problem for the Eagles is that they've struggled to stop the pass this year and they're facing a Panthers team that is SECOND in the NFL in passing yards per game. I never thought in my entire life that I'd type out anything like that about Carolina's offense, but here we are. The deck is stacked against the Eagles, so I have no choice here; I'm taking the Panthers. PICK: Panthers (+1.5) 27-24 over Eagles However, the Eagles are far from healthy going into Sunday's matchup with the Panthers. Their offensive line is battered by injuries, their right tackle Lane Johnson just suddenly retired and they're down to their practice-squad running backs. Carolina has plenty of injury issues of their own , but at least one analyst thinks they can pull off a win this week. John Breech at CBS Sports is predicting a victory for the Panthers: It's not a wild take given the situation. In fact, they were one Xavier Legette drop away from upsetting the Eagles the last time they visited Philly two years ago. Plus, the Eagles' struggling offense may not be able to take advantage of what might be the Panthers' biggest weakness—their banged-up cornerback room. Even without starters Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, Carolina might not have too difficult of a time keeping down the league's fifth-worst passing attack—especially if it's still missing their top wideout in DeVonta Smith. away.blurb: The Eagles welcomed the return of four players on Injured Reserve back to the practice field, but running back Saquon Barkley remained sidelined. The Eagles opened the practice window for four players currently on Injured Reserve on Wednesday – cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra (back), guard Landon Dickerson (knee), and tight end Eli Stowers (quad). All four were limited on Wednesday. "Happy to be back at practice. Glad to be back out there. Feeling good and healthy," Dickerson said. "I feel a lot better than I did back in Week 1." Wide receiver Hollywood Brown (ankle) and safety Marcus Epps (groin) also returned to practice on Wednesday in a limited capacity, as did outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard (ankle). Brown has been sidelined since suffering the injury during the preparation for Week 3 in Chicago. Epps suffered his injury one week later in practice. Greenard didn't practice at all last week, but was questionable and a game-time decision before ultimately not being able to play. The Carolina Panthers, who are coming off of a bye week, did not practice on Wednesday, so their injury report was an estimate. Starting right tackle, rookie Monroe Freeling, would not have practiced due to a knee injury. DB Jakorian Bennett, TE Grant Calcaterra, G Landon Dickerson, and TE Eli Stowers return to practice from Injured Reserve. Neither practiced on Wednesday, along with defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen), outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle), center Drew Kendall (knee), and running back Will Shipley (foot). Dickerson is the only one of the four who has played in a game this season. He started the season opener against Washington and then went on Injured Reserve. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot,” the Eagles’ statement said . “Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia.” “On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday’s game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority,” the Eagles added . As of this writing, it isn’t clear how long Hurts is going to be out. Hopefully the situation isn’t as scary as it sounds and Hurts will be OK. While the Eagles have not yet officially announced their starter for Week 6 with Hurts out, it will almost certainly be Tanner McKee. The Philadelphia Eagles won’t have the services of quarterback Jalen Hurts for the Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers. The Eagles noted that Hurts first requested treatment for his calf issue on Oct. 8, and an ultrasound on Saturday revealed a small blood clot, but Hurts ended up playing versus Jacksonville. Then, the Eagles performed another ultrasound on Wednesday night and it revealed there was movement in the blood clot, which led to the decision to sit Hurts for Week 6. MORE: NFL insider believes Jalen Hurts’ future could be big offseason story The Eagles noted that Hurts informed the training staff he had been cleated in his calf during the game against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4, which is what appears to have led to the issue he’s dealing with now. home.headline: Concerns Grow as Eagles' First Week 6 Injury Report Includes a Third of the Team
home.blurb: There were 17 players listed either as not participating or limited participants. That’s darn near a third of the team. Things can only get better as the week goes on, right? At least quarterback Jalen Hurts wasn’t on it. The Eagles didn’t list the QB on their injury report until last Friday, just before boarding a plane to London. He was trying to get loose. That could explain why he ran just twice for two yards in the loss to the Jaguars, and the Eagles didn’t try a tush push in short-yardage situations. So, maybe that’s good news for Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers, because there have to be some worries with an injury report the length of an arm. Smith was counted on to be the team’s No. 1 receiver this season after A.J. Brown was traded, but he missed the previous two games. home.blurb: "Breaking: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts is out for Sunday due to a superficial blood clot," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport wrote on his official X account on Thursday. "Eagles QB Jalen Hurts is OUT for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers due to a superficial blood clot in his calf," The 33rd Team's Ari Meirov wrote on his official X account. "The team says the clot was discovered Saturday in London, but doctors cleared him to play against the Jaguars . A follow-up ultrasound Wednesday revealed that the clot had moved, prompting the team to rule him out as doctors determine the appropriate treatment." Hurts out means backup quarterback Tanner McKee will make his third career start against the Panthers. McKee is 1-1 in his previous two starts — he started the regular-season finale in 2024 and again in 2025. The franchise announced the news about Hurts in a lengthy statement posted to their official social media accounts: "On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf. He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report. Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia. Jalen played without limitation in the game Sunday, received treatment on Monday and Tuesday, and practiced in full on Wednesday, as reflected in the practice report. Throughout our time in London and this week, we have remained in communication with the league office regarding the matter. On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority." Eagles' Jalen Hurts Injury Update: Why QB Won't Play vs. Panthers Unlock the latest Heavy on Eagles news — direct to your inbox. In a move that could drastically alter the season for the Philadelphia Eagles , the team announced on Thursday that starting quarterback and Super Bowl MVP Jalen Hurts won't play in Sunday's Week 7 game against the Carolina Panthers after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his leg. "A scary situation for Eagles QB Jalen Hurts," NFL Network's Mike Garafolo wrote on his official X account. Yes. Yes. Let me say it again: Yes. After a horror show in Week 4 with my NFL picks , I got back on track in a big way this past week. I was 10-4-1 straight up and 9-6-1 against the spread. That brings my season record straight up to 48-30-1 and the ATS record to 34-43-2. The ATS mark will be a slow climb to get back above .500 after that really bad Week 3. But I felt good about the picks this week. Time to build some momentum. Two good weeks in a row? All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Seattle Seahawks (-3) at Denver Broncos Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Seahawks lost a tough one to the 49ers last week and now face a short week on the road against Denver. The Broncos ' offense has struggled, even with Sean Payton taking over as the play-caller. Bo Nix has to pick it up, but this is a tough defense to try and fix things. Seattle takes a tough road game. Pick: Seahawks 23, Broncos 17 Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) London on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Jaguars will have been in London for two weeks, which makes this a challenge for the Texans , who went this week. Houston won for the first time on the road last week and now their division chances probably rest on this game. The Jaguars were sloppy last week, which will get them back focused. Jaguars will win a tight one. Pick: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons (+3) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a horrible showing in Green Bay, in which the defense was shredded. But the Falcons lost in overtime to the Ravens and quarterback Michael Penix was hurt. He will likely play here, and that's a good thing since he can light up the Chicago defense. Falcons win it. Pick: Falcons 27, Bears 21 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns There is a chance that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be back for this game after missing last week with an ankle injury. Even if he isn't, I think the Ravens defense will be up to the task of slowing down the Browns offense. If Jackson is back, the Ravens offense will move the ball. Pick: Ravens 24, Browns 13 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts (-7) The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game. Pick: Colts 28, Titans 17 New York Jets at New England Patriots (-7.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Patriots have turned their season around with consecutive victories as Drake Maye has come alive. The Jets played better on defense against Cleveland last week with eight sacks, but this is a bigger challenge. Look for Maye to keep it going as the Pats win a third straight. Pick: Patriots 28, Jets 13 New Orleans Saints at New York Giants (+1.5) The Saints have lost three straight and have fallen to 1-4. They didn't play well against the Vikings last week, but this is a chance to get right. The Giants tied last week, but Jameis Winston played well. I think this will be about defenses. Giants in a close one. Pick: Giants 19, Saints 16 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense. Pick: Eagles 23, Panthers 20 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3) Both of these teams righted the ship a bit with victories last week. The Bucs badly needed it after losing their first four. Tampa Bay ran it with Bucky Irving to beat the Cowboys and I think they can do that here as well. The defense played better in that game and will limit Aaron Rodgers somewhat. Bucs win it. Pick: Bucs 26, Steelers 21 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams (-13.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The "Dream Team" Rams are 2-3 and haven't looked the part of a Super Bowl champ. The offense got it going against the Bills , but the defense was a non-factor in the fourth quarter and overtime. They will play better here against the Cardinals . Meanwhile, Matt Stafford will have a big day. Pick: Rams 35, Cardinals 20 Los Angeles Chargers (+8.5) at Kansas City Chiefs Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chargers limp into this one at 0-5, while the Chiefs are undefeated off a bye. The Chargers are desperate and need a win or their season will be over. This is not a good place to try to get that first victory. Look for Patrick Mahomes to play well. Chiefs coach Andy Reid is outstanding in his career off a bye. Pick: Chiefs 28, Chargers 21 Buffalo Bills (-6) at Las Vegas Raiders The Bills are playing consecutive road games, but they stayed on the West Coast after beating the Rams in overtime Monday night. That was a tough, physical game, which will make it a challenge on a short week. The Raiders were awful against the Pats, but they will play better on offense here. They just won't stop the Bills. Pick: Bills 35, Raiders 21 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Packers blew out the Bears Sunday as Jordan Love lit up the skies. Look for more of that in this one against a bad Dallas secondary. The Cowboys struggled on defense against the Bucs, and that will continue in this one. Love continues to play well. Packers win a shootout. Pick: Packers 31, Cowboys 27 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a long road trip for the Commanders off a brutal tie last week to face the league's best team right now. That's a tough combination. They can only hope for a letdown by the 49ers after they beat Seattle last week. It won't happen. The 49ers continue to roll as Brock Purdy continues to make a claim as a legitimate MVP candidate. away.headline: Could Baker Mayfield return in Week 6 game vs. Steelers?
away.blurb: Mayfield, who suffered a dislocated thumb on his right throwing hand on September 27, was expected to miss three to six weeks as he recovered from his injury. As expected, Mayfield began the Week 6 practice report as a non-participant, casting doubt on a miraculous return against Pittsburgh one week early. Drafted by the Browns with the first overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft, Mayfield played four seasons with Cleveland (2018-2021), in addition to brief stints with the Carolina Panthers (2022) and Los Angeles Rams (2022), before joining the Buccaneers in 2023, where he had a career resurgence. Mayfield has appeared in 126 games and made 123 starts over his nine-year NFL career. He has thrown for 29,140 passing yards and 199 touchdowns, as well as earning two Pro Bowl selections. With Mayfield potentially sidelined, the Buccaneers will call on undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels to make his second career start. Daniels led Tampa Bay to its first win of the season in last week's game against the Dallas Cowboys, but a Steelers team riding the momentum of a huge win over the Indianapolis Colts may be a different story. away.headline: Report: Steelers WR Roman Wilson (finger) to miss multiple weeks
away.blurb: Wilson had no catches on one target before exiting in the second quarter of the 34-22 win. He was grabbing his left hand after an incompletion and did not return to the game. ESPN reported that Wilson is still gathering more information about the injury and will seek a second opinion. Wilson, a third-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft by Pittsburgh, has 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns in five games this season. The 25-year-old has 26 receptions for 354 yards and four TDs over the last two seasons for the Steelers. Wilson’s status comes after Pittsburgh placed wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on injured reserve Saturday and Ben Skowronek also left Sunday’s game with a calf injury. away.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." home.headline: Myles Garrett could make Rams return next week, per report
home.blurb: Garrett’s knee issue initially began causing problems during training camp, creating uncertainty surrounding his availability and ability to perform at his usual level. Although the veteran defensive end has continued working toward a return, the lingering issue has complicated his path back to full strength. The Rams have taken a cautious approach to his recovery, prioritizing his long-term health rather than rushing him back before he is ready. Garrett’s return timeline became clearer this week when Rapoport discussed the situation during an appearance on The Rich Eisen Show. According to Rapoport, Garrett was given a recovery timeline of approximately six weeks following knee surgery . With the procedure taking place the Monday after the season opener, Week 7 represents a realistic target for his return. However, head coach Sean McVay indicated that Garrett would not return to practice this week, leaving some uncertainty surrounding the exact timetable. Although Week 7 remains the most recent update, the Rams will need to ensure Garrett is “return to performance” not just “return to play”. The team needs the Myles Garrett they acquired, not a version that is playing with limitations or at a limited capacity. The Los Angeles Rams could get back Myles Garrett as soon as next week against the Las Vegas Raiders, according to NFL insider Ian Rapoport. Garrett’s potential availability would provide a significant lift for a Rams team that is 2-3 and facing another midseason “must-win” stretch after a slow start. Garrett has not played since Week 1, missing four games since he went on IR with a knee injury following arthroscopic surgery. Even though the decision came late, after the team’s week 1 loss to San Francisco, it was the right decision as the team pursues a Super Bowl with the combination of Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald. Garrett recorded zero tackles in his first game with the Rams in Week 1 against the 49ers. He had an NFL record 23 sacks in 2025 with the Cleveland Browns and 125.5 career sacks en total. Garrett had hoped to have even more sacks in 2026 , but now L.A.’s only goal is to get him back in one piece.

The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. Looking at the Chiefs' Week 6 matchup, Kansas City is taking on one of the worst teams in the league, record-wise. The Chargers are coming off their fifth straight loss, most recently at the hands of the Denver Broncos. Golden J starts this conversation praising LA's quarterback Justin Herbert, who he believes is still a great QB but has no supporting cast around him this season. With that being said, this is a game that the Chiefs should have zero issue winning. With the extra week of rest, dominant performances in the first four games, home-field advantage and a Chargers team that is seemingly completely hopeless, Kansas City is walking into a recipe for a win. With that said, the Chiefs can't overlook LA. The Chargers are still a professional football team and there's no situation where an NFL team can take its foot off the gas. Looking at the Chiefs' week off, the team did not sign or trade for an NFL-ready wide receiver despite Tyquan Thornton hitting the injured list with a dislocated ankle. Tight end Travis Kelce leads the team in receiving yards, but Thornton is a close second. There's hope that Thornton can return for the playoffs, but he'll be out for an extended period of time regardless. Head coach Andy Reid mentioned that rookie WR Cyrus Allen might be in the mix a bit more with Thornton's absence but the team does still boast a talented receiving corps consisting of Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and the Swiss Army knife of a TE, Kelce. Ex-Chiefs WR Tyreek Hill was initially believed to be back in KC, but his ongoing legal battle may complicate things. There hasn't been much on that front as of late, but a reunion is still on the table as long as he remains a free agent. Golden J and Chico breifly discuss a trade that could have been, with the Arizona Cardinals moving Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans. Whether there was a possibility of Harrison landing with the Chiefs is unknown, but a thought to explore. Kansas City did bring on Justin Watson to their practice squad Monday, though there has been no subsequent move to elevate him to the game-day squad. Watson was previously with the Chiefs from 2022-2024, so he should be relatively familiar with their playbook.

Justin Herbert hasn't played well enough to overcome the problems around him, and Arrowhead isn't where I'd expect everything to suddenly click. Kansas City can lean on Kenneth Walker III without asking Mahomes to do all the heavy lifting. If the Chargers slow the run, there's still the small matter of defending the quarterback. I'm not blindly betting on an Andy Reid bye-week trend. I'm looking at two teams playing very different levels of football. The Chiefs take control early and leave the Chargers desperate for answers heading into their bye. home.blurb: Included in the list of injured players were starting left tackle Joe Alt (neck, DNP), star safety Derwin James Jr. (hamstring, DNP) and leading wide receivers Ladd McConkey (foot, limited participant) and Quentin Johnston (chest, limited). At wide receiver, Los Angeles is dealing with a plethora of issues. (KCTV) - A wounded and winless Los Angeles Chargers team is headed toward Kansas City this weekend looking to hand the Chiefs their first loss of the season. But those aforementioned wounds are mounting after five weeks of play, and Wednesday’s injury report shared by head coach Jim Harbaugh’s team was a lengthy one. In total, nearly 40 percent of the Chargers’ active roster were listed with some ailment after their first practice of the week. Not included on the injury report was Chargers center Tyler Biadasz, who was placed on season-ending injured reserve in August due to a torn ACL suffered in training camp and starting right tackle Rashawn Slater and backup Trey Pipkins, who were each placed on injured reserve in recent weeks due to ankle and knee issues. As a result, last week, injuries on the Chargers offensive line led to multiple rookies starting for Los Angeles in a game where star quarterback Justin Herbert was sacked five times. All of those injuries to Chargers pass-catchers, which include tight end David Njoku being placed on injured reserve in September, resulted in the Chargers hosting several wide receivers for tryouts on Tuesday and signing former Raymore-Peculiar and KU alum Luke Grimm to their practice squad.
