picks.headline: Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6
picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Eagles QB Jalen Hurts out for Week 6 due to superficial blood clot TRENDING Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 Tim Crean, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:44 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Buffalo Bills face off against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. This matchup between the 4-1 Bills and the 3-2 Raiders gets a prime spot in the late Sunday window as one of the best games of the week. These two original AFC franchises haven't played a game with meaningful stakes for both teams since the 1993 "Just Freeze Baby" Divisional Round game . Now, as both sides come into this game with winning records, let's make some bold Bills-Raiders predictions. Start your Raiders in fantasy football The Bills are their own worst enemy so far this season, as they love to gift their opponents chances to stay in the game. Whether it is shockingly cavalier Josh Allen interceptions, infuriating James Cook fumbles, or the fact that the defense (outside of Deone Walker and Gregory Rousseau) looks like it has no clue what it is doing right now, Buffalo loves keeping the other team in the game. Sunday will be no different, as fans should expect at least two turnovers from the Bills' offense and long stretches where the Raiders' O looks like the 2007 New England Patriots. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That means big games from the Raiders' defense, Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty, and maybe even the likes of Mike Washington Jr., Michael Mayer, and Tre Tucker. So, for all you fantasy football players out there, any Raiders on your roster should be a good play in Week 6 . Josh Allen delivers again Despite the mediocre (or worse) play at times from the Bills' offensive line, wide receivers, tight end, and running backs, and defensive back seven, the Bills are 4-1 and leading the AFC East thanks to one man: Brandon Beane. Just kidding! He's the reason the rest of the team is struggling so much. The real reason is Josh Allen. Through five weeks, Allen is still the betting favorite for NFL MVP this year. Yes, Brock Bowers is playing great, and Patrick Mahomes is back, but if you define MVP as the players whose absence would tank his team's chances the most, Allen has to be the answer. Monday night's dramatic OT win over the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams came courtesy of 210 yards passing and a staggering 121 yards rushing from the Bills QB. Sure, he threw his obligatory head-scratching pick in the first half, but in the second, it was a one-man battle with 53 Rams players, and the singular man won. Against the Raiders, expect more of the same. Vegas has an improved defense this season and an incredible pass rusher in Maxx Crosby, but that only means Allen will be forced to take off even more as usual. And with his receivers getting minimal separation and Cook's suspect ball security, it will be all Allen, all the time in Week 6. Bills 31, Raiders 24 This won't be a cakewalk for the Bills by any means, as the Raiders are one of (if not) the most improved teams in the league. We know Cousins is a professional QB, the Raiders have some incredible young offensive weapons, and Klint Kubiak seems like a legit NFL head coach with an incredibly bright future. Allen doesn't have those last two things, as his skill position core is the exact same as last year, as long as D.J. Moore is out injured and his "new" head coach is just the same offensive coordinator who couldn't get it done the past three seasons, but with a more impressive title. Nevertheless, Allen should be able to will his Bills to victory over the Raiders in Week 6 just by sheer force of talent and will. As good as Las Vegas has looked at times this season, they are probably a year or two away from being legit contenders. That's why we'll take the Buffalo to win here, and to do so by slightly more than the -5.5-point spread suggests. Stop me if you've heard this one before, but Buffalo has one of the NFL's best offenses behind Josh Allen and it doesn't seem like there's a defense in the league that's going to be able to stop this team from scoring 30 points — they're quite literally averaging 32.7 points per game after the first five games of the year. Meanwhile, the Raiders have certainly fallen back to earth a bit, losing two straight after their 3-0 start to the season. At the same time, the Bills defense is the same problem it's been for the past few years. Easiest NFL Week 6 pick on the board Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5) Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5) This line could've been two touchdowns and I'm still taking the Kansas City Chiefs over the division rival Chargers. For starters, what has LA shown this season to make you believe they have a chance in Arrowhead in Week 6? No, seriously. There's been little evidence to think that this game will be close as the Chiefs have been absolutely rolling on both sides of the ball while Justin Herbert delivers the worst season of his career, the Chargers defense is middling at its best and the self-inflicted wounds in each game from LA multiply likes the heads of a hydra. If that weren't enough, Andy Reid is famously one of the most lethal head coaches when his team is coming off of the bye week. This isn't to say that the Chiefs are a perfect team as I maintain that they still need to find some more upgrades at wide receiver, especially after the gnarly Tyquan Thornton injury. While that may be true, though, they are a far better coached and more talented team than the winless Chargers and I wouldn't be surprised if this game was lopsided and out of hand early in favor of the home side. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers Coming off of a home loss to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and the previously winless Buccaneers, naturally I'm taking the Dallas Cowboys to go on the road to Lambeau and beat the Packers as underdogs. What about this doesn't make sense to you? Yes, the optics look strange. However, this isn't about expecting the Cowboys hiring Mike Pettine to essentially help out new defensive coordinator Christian Parker drastically improving the defense, though it can't hurt. It's more about this being a likely shootout between these two teams because, despite what happened to Tyson Bagent and the Bears, I still don't trust Green Bay on that side of the ball. Furthermore, I also still don't trust the Packers run game, even against Dallas. Expect this game to go back and forth throughout the action, but I believe the Cowboys are going to have more offensive firepower and some adjustments on the side of the ball you can actually trust Dallas on to attack Green Bay throughout. They might not come up with many stops of their own, but they'll have enough to pull out the win. Plus, just from a narrative perspective, if ever there was a time for the Cowboys to keep their fans from abandoning ship, it's a game like this, and this franchise has been masterful at doing exactly that over the years. picks.headline: Week 6 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Packers had much different results last week
picks.blurb: Week 6 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Packers had much different results last week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Eagles QB Jalen Hurts out for Week 6 due to superficial blood clot TRENDING Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 15, 2026 at 2:37 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One week can change the entire perception of an NFL team — sometimes that's good, sometimes it's not. The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers were both 2-2 coming into last week's games. The Cowboys weren't considered a Super Bowl contender, but they were at least looking OK — especially in a bad NFC East — with a home game against the winless Buccaneers coming up. The Packers had played so poorly through four weeks that they were home underdogs to the Bears for the first time in 20 years , even though Chicago was starting its backup quarterback. The Cowboys and Packers come into Week 6's Sunday night game with their seasons flipped around. The Cowboys looked horrible against the Buccaneers, losing to an undrafted rookie quarterback in Jalon Daniels. The defensive problems finally got to a point in which the Cowboys hired longtime NFL defensive coordinator Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant and said defensive coordinator Christian Parker will now call plays from the press box. There's always some angst in Dallas because of the attention on the Cowboys all the time, but it's not like the defensive problems are made up. Dallas was last in defensive DVOA last season and they're last so far this season. Meanwhile, the talk of Matt LaFleur being on the hot seat seems like it was a lot longer than a week ago. The best way to gain back the confidence of Packers fans is to blow out the Bears, and the Packers did just that. They blasted Chicago, 31-7, with Jordan Love embarrassing the Bears defense with his deep passing and Green Bay shutting down everything Chicago's offense wanted to do. After not playing a good game through four weeks, the Packers played a great game in Week 5. That makes Week 6 hard to figure out. Do the Cowboys rebound or is the defense simply unfixable? What's the real Packers team — the one that couldn't run the ball, couldn't protect Love and had a below-average defense through four games, or the one we saw Sunday? The Packers are small favorites Sunday night, indicating the oddsmakers don't have a lot of confidence in them still. But it's tougher to bank on the Cowboys' defense. Packers -1.5 is the pick , though it could all look different for both teams next week. That's how the NFL goes. The Green Bay Packers' MarShawn Lloyd celebrates a touchdown with the fans at Lambeau Field last week. (AP Photo/Nam Huh) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 6 of the NFL season: Seahawks (-2.5) over Broncos Not all is great for the defending champs, who can't run the ball and still don't have an offensive option other than Jaxon Smith-Njigba. But they've been far better than the Broncos, who were on their way to losing to the winless and injury-plagued Chargers before saving themselves with a fourth-quarter rally. The matchup of Seattle's defense against an aimless Broncos offense is enough to take the Seahawks. Jaguars (-2.5) over Texans A bit of a weird line. The Jaguars are 4-1 and while last week's miracle win over the Eagles wasn't great, they do look like a legitimate contender in the AFC. The Texans are 1-4 and their lone win came against the 0-5 Titans. And yet, in a neutral site game — if either team has the edge it's Jacksonville, who does the London trip every season and stayed overseas after playing there last week — the Jaguars aren't even giving a full field goal. Yes it's a desperate Houston team with a very good defense, but it's not a lot of respect for the Jaguars. Falcons (+1.5) over Bears It appears Michael Penix Jr. and Caleb Williams will start, which should make for an entertaining game. The big question for this one will be what to make of the Bears defense. In Week 1 and 5 they gave up 68 combined points. From Weeks 2-4 they allowed 28 points. The hot stretch in the middle could have come from facing three bad offenses (Vikings without Kyler Murray in bad weather, Eagles, Jets) instead of the Panthers and Packers, their other two opponents who both scored more than 30 points. The Falcons are a good offense with Penix, so points should be coming. Browns (+5.5) over Ravens The Ravens should have confidence after beating the Falcons without Lamar Jackson last week. However, a Tyler Huntley offense still isn't one I'm comfortable laying 5.5 points with on the road. Buccaneers (+2.5) over Steelers Metrics like DVOA and net EPA per play say these teams are practically even. The Buccaneers have the rest advantage, having played last Thursday night, and the Steelers are 0-2 on the road (3-0 at home). Daniels could be exposed by the best defense he's faced, but it's also not the intimidating Steelers defense from recent years. Patriots (-7.5) over Jets The Patriots are officially warmed up. The start to the season was lackluster, but Drake Maye is coming off two good games in a row. The Jets are better than some expected, but they're facing a team that has its season back on track and wants to keep that going. Bet the New England Patriots to cover the spread at sportsbooks Giants (+1.5) over Saints It's hard to buy the Giants. There's no evidence they're a good team despite their 3-1-1 record. But it's not like there are any signs that the Saints are much better. New Orleans is 30th in DVOA ahead of only the hopeless Titans and Dolphins. Anything can happen when Jameis Winston is starting at quarterback, good or bad — good luck predicting it. Panthers (-1) over Eagles It's weird to see the Panthers favored at Philadelphia (though some books have the Eagles as a small favorite). But to this point, Carolina has been the far better team. Also, they're coming off a bye while the Eagles come right off a flight from London, where they took a horrific loss after kicking a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left. Colts (-7) over Titans The Titans should be very happy the Dolphins exist, or else there would be even more talk about how bad they are. Indianapolis hasn't been great, either, but it's just too difficult to take the Titans right now. Cardinals (+12.5) over Rams It's quite possible the Rams take out their frustrations on the Cardinals. Los Angeles is 2-3, but the schedule has been tough and it starts to ease up with a game against Arizona, which just got throttled by the Lions. The Cardinals seem to be running out of steam after looking decent to start the season. Still, 12.5 points is a lot considering the Rams haven't looked great yet, and Arizona can move the ball, especially in garbage time. Raiders (+5.5) over Bills The Bills are coming off an emotional, difficult overtime win against the Rams on Monday night. They are the better team, but that's a tough situational spot, and the Raiders are not as bad as they looked last week against the Patriots. Let's give Vegas one more shot to show that 3-0 start wasn't fraudulent. Chiefs (-8) over Chargers The Chargers aren't just bad, they're injured. They held their own against the Broncos last week, but that probably says more about Denver. This season is already ugly for Los Angeles and it's not going to get much better. Commanders (+7.5) over 49ers If the Commanders aren't completely downtrodden after one of the dumbest endings in recent NFL history last week, in which they casually watched the final minute of overtime run out without getting a field-goal attempt, then this seems like too many points. The 49ers have played very well on both sides of the ball (the defense has been a great surprise), but there is some danger of a letdown after winning at Seattle. Take the points and hope last week's fiasco doesn't still linger for Washington. Last week: 5-9-1 Season to date: 34-43-2

away.blurb: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts out for Week 6 due to superficial blood clot Caleb's return won't solve it all Now, to add insult to injury, the NFL is punishing two Cowboys players for their actions in Week 4 of the NFL season. NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL TRENDING Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week Anne Erickson Sat, October 10, 2026 at 9:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys fell 24-16 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on "Thursday Night Football" to kick off the NFL's Week 5 festivities, and it wasn't a good look for the franchise. The main reason this loss was rough is because the Cowboys fell to a 0-4 Buccaneers team that has undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels subbing for the injured Baker Mayfield. You know something is wrong when you're losing to an undrafted free agent, but in all seriousness, Daniels was impressive. So, it could be more about his impressive showing than the Cowboys tanking, but still, this franchise is already on the clock to turn things around this season. Two Cowboys players fined by the NFL "Player infractions may come to the league's attention in a variety of ways. The league may respond to an official's call during a game or to a specific play that a team submits for review," the league notes. In this weekend's report, the NFL slaps Cowboys player Reddy Steward with a $5,583 fine for unnecessary roughness due to a hit on a defenseless player at 10:57 in the third quarter, as well as Kavontae Turpin with an $11,941 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct due to taunting at 10:50 in the third quarter. So, it's just a bit more bad news for two guys playing for a franchise that's hurting. But it's still early in the season, so the Cowboys have lots of time to come back. away.blurb: Shedeur Sanders could have another NFL team to consider if the Cleveland Browns decide to move him before the trade deadline. The Dallas Cowboys have emerged as a possible destination for the young quarterback, with CBS Sports analyst John Breech identifying Dallas as one of five teams that could pursue a deal. Sanders has struggled to find regular playing time in Cleveland this season, while the Cowboys already have Dak Prescott firmly established as their starter. The reported link raises an interesting question: could Dallas see value in developing Sanders as a long-term backup rather than letting his potential go to waste? Cowboys named as a potential trade destination for Shedeur Sanders Breech pointed to the connection between Sanders' father, Deion Sanders, and the Cowboys as one reason the move could attract attention. Sanders could fill a similar developmental role, although his career has followed a different path. Dallas currently has Sam Howell behind Prescott. Acquiring Sanders could give the Cowboys another option to evaluate, especially if they believe he still has room to grow. away.blurb: The Buccaneers will be without QB Baker Mayfield for a second straight game and have a new issue on defense with Antoine Winfield Jr. ruled out, but rookie OLB Rueben Bain Jr. and TE Ko Kieft are back after missing time Linebacker SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) are also inactive for Thursday's game due to injuries. Tight end Ko Kieft, who missed one game due to an elbow issue, is also back in action. home.headline: Micah Parsons provides promising injury update for Packers fans
home.blurb: Micah Parsons, out since last December with a torn ACL, is nearing his comeback for the Packers as they look to bounce back from a slow start in the NFC North, winners of two games in a row. Around 9.5 months after his surgery last December, Parsons is nearing a return, but it won't come in Week 6 against his former Cowboys squad. He has yet to return to practice, and remains on Green Bay's PUP list as the team waits for him to be medically cleared. But it shouldn't be too long before that happens. "The biggest thing that people worried about with me, they're like, 'Man, why ain't he back yet?'" Parsons said. "If the Super Bowl was this week, I'm playing in the Super Bowl. But it's just about me making sure I have all the small things fixed first. What a lot of people don't figure out is it's not just the ACL. It's like, why did the ACL happen? What was weak? Because it all works together. It's a chain. And throughout the history of ACL, they notice if you come back early, there tends to be an overcompensation injury on the other side." Previously, he said he thought a return to face the Cowboys in Week 6 was "realistic," but it won't materialize as hoped. It won't be long before one of the NFL's premiere pass rushers is back on the field. Parsons provided the latest update on his timeline on his podcast recently, saying he's in the final stages of making sure his knee will hold up. Here's what Parsons said about his injury outlook. MORE: The Sporting News' latest 2027 NFL Mock Draft Micah Parsons provides injury update Parsons said on the latest episode of his podcast, "The Edge With Micah Parsons," that if it was a do-or-die game, he'd be ready to play, but has preferred to play it safe with his longer timeline. The star pass rusher said he wants to make sure he's fully at 100% before he returns. "It's like, what's the point of getting me back for four weeks and then next thing you know, my groin [is] bothering me," Parsons said. "So many people wanted me to be back for that game to make the game bigger than what it was," Parsons said on his podcast. "It's just another 'Sunday Night Football' game between two good teams. It's not about me. I think that probably let people down. 'Oh, Micah, he's gonna want to be back for the Dallas game.' No, I'm in that phase of life where I just want to be healthy again. That's it." For now, Parsons is waiting to be cleared so he can begin his ramp up to play. It won't be happening this week, but soon, the Packers will be getting a game-changing weapon back for their defense. They will have a challenge against the 49ers' offense, who are No. 8 in rushing yards per game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Look for the Commanders to slow, not stop, Christian McCaffrey. However, that opens things up for the 49ers' passing attack to hit high gear. The biggest problem the Commanders will have is Mike Evans. That's not a deep analysis. It's something every team faces when playing the 49ers. Purdy said Evans makes a big difference , according to ESPN. "He's a game changer," Purdy said after the win over the Seahawks. "True X receiver that, if you get the right look and stuff and you give him a chance, he can make defenses pay. "I thought today he did a great job with that, going up and getting the ball multiple times and just using his length and everything to create some separation. So as a quarterback, any time I have an (opportunity) to go to him, it always feels good." Evans doesn't shy away from the attention. And why should he? He's a future Hall of Famer. "I do feel like I'm one of the best receivers in the game," Evans said. "I got a big frame, so if you throw it around me, I'm going to do my best to try to make those contested grabs." The 49ers won't have Deebo Samuel, who suffered a hamstring injury against the Seahawks. That could allow the Commanders to focus more attention on Evans. But the 49ers still have threats, including George Kittle. And even Kittle has major respect for Evans, according to a post on X. "Mike Evans is really good at football," Kittle posted. 49ers TE George Kittle will have a season-high reception total Kittle's best game came in Week 3 against the Cardinals as he grabbed six passes for 82 yards and a pair of scores. Look for him to have a similar line against the Commanders with Samuel on the shelf. The 49ers have Kittle, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, and Jacob Cowing on the roster. And that's enough , said head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to ESPN. "I think we have enough," Shanahan said. "We've got three guys on practice squad also who can help. I mean, anytime you lose this number of guys, whether it's four guys or five guys, whatever it is, it's a huge challenge. But we do have guys in this building who can do it, and we'll always look." Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will finally cross 200-yard passing mark In three games this season, Daniels hasn't totaled over 200 yards passing. Look for that to change against the 49ers. It makes sense for the 49ers to focus defensively on keeping Daniels in check as a runner. He's coming off a game where he ran for 103 yards on nine carries and a pair of touchdowns. And look for the Commanders' game plan to lean more on the passing game than it has so far this season. Part of it will likely be from necessity as the Commanders figure to be chasing points throughout this game. Daniels has a lot to prove after his late-game blunder against the Giants. He has tried to own the situation , according to ESPN. "We have to stop the clock," Daniels said. "We have to know the situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it's on me." A bounce-back game against the 49ers by Daniels won't help Quinn's future as head coach. But it would be an olive branch to Commanders' fans who are furious about Daniels' mental meltdown. Commanders WR Terry McLaurin will get a long TD Look for the Commanders to strike deep against the 49ers. McLaurin should be the beneficiary with a 40-plus-yard score. McLaurin hasn't been anything special from a fantasy perspective this season. He had catch totals of 2, 2, 6, and 4 in his first four games. He has 203 total yards and one touchdown. Those aren't WR1 numbers. He is playing like a pedestrian blob so far this season. And while he probably won't juice up those numbers much against the 49ers' tough defense, it's not out of the realm of possibility for him to get a deep ball. How big of an ask is a 40-yard TD strike between Daniels and McLaurin? Consider that Daniels' longest pass of the season is 33 yards. McLaurin's longest catch is 30 yards. Those numbers seem to belie the likelihood of a long hookup. However, the 49ers can't fear the deep ball because of this duo's modest production. And that's why there's a window of opportunity for a bomb. However, look for the Commanders to fall to 1-4-1 after this one. They don't have the roster to compete with the 49ers. That's a plus for the Commanders, who formally opened his 21-day window to return off injured reserve. He was placed on IR following a hamstring strain suffered in a Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. He's an important depth piece and core special teams player who was missed while he was out. Magee should be the primary backup if he's able to return off IR. If he isn't activated before the end of this 21-day window, he'll be placed on season-ending injured reserve. The Commanders have return to play guidelines that generally involved a ramp-up period, though it varies in length based upon the nature of the injury and a player's health status. Getting Magee before a Week 6 clash with San Francisco is probably an unfair expectation, but it's not impossible. A return after the bye, though, seems more likely. away.headline: Commanders' injury report gives Giants a leg up in Week 5, even with Jayden Daniels
away.blurb: In fact, Big Blue might be the healthier team on Sunday. The Washington Commanders are dealing with a long list of injuries, even with Jayden Daniels likely set to return to the field. His teammates, on the other hand, have not had such an encouraging week. His top two receivers, Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, did not participate in practice on Wednesday or Thursday. McLaurin participated in a limited capacity on Friday, but Diggs did not. Both wideouts are dealing with hamstring injuries. If McLaurin and Diggs are both out, Washington will be left with Dyami Brown, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, and Luke McCaffrey as its only healthy receivers. Commanders' injury report gives Giants a leg up in Week 5, even with Jayden Daniels Skip to main content News It may feel like the New York Giants are the most injured team in the NFL. They are not. Losing Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns, among others, for the season was a devastating blow, but the G-Men still have enough healthy talent on both sides of the ball to remain competitive, especially in a wide-open NFC East. With key commanders missing from the lineup, the Giants have an important advantage in what has become a crucial game in the NFC East title race. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs headline Commanders' injury report vs. Giants Daniels was a full participant in Commanders practice on both Wednesday and Thursday. Barring an unexpected change over the weekend, he should be able to play for the first time since injuring his elbow in Week 2. Of course, the Giants have some important injuries of their own. Braxton Berrios is now set to miss the season with a foot injury. Chauncey Golston's neck injury could leave New York thin on the edge, and safety Jason Pinnock is dealing with a concussion. But in terms of new names popping up on the injury report, the Giants certainly have the advantage in this game. Commanders' injury report gives Giants a clear advantage in Week 5 The Giants' secondary hasn't been stellar this season. The pass defense has been average in most categories and has been torn apart by the most efficient passing offenses it has faced. But if Washington is without its top two wide receivers, New York's secondary should be able to take control of the game. Deonte Banks, who has been a full participant in practice this week , and Greg Newsome II can lock Brown and Burks down on the outside while Dru Phillips handles Williams in the slot. If the Giants limit the Commanders' rushing attack, which hasn't been particularly efficient this year, they can put this game away early.

Schefter described the situation as "a matter of when, not if" Daniels suffers another injury to his left elbow. "Daniels visited specialists in New York and Los Angeles, and the overwhelming opinion was that playing with a brace was a viable option," wrote Schefter. By Michael Gallagher Sports Content Coordinator 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The San Francisco 49ers have had arguably the worst injury luck of any team in the NFL this season. More than 15 players are currently on the reserve/injured list while a handful of others are expected to miss some time with their respective ailments. San Francisco’s defense has been hit particularly hard, and star edge-rusher Nick Bosa’s absence over the last few weeks has been noticeable. Keion White has done his part to pick up the slack, but the rest of San Francisco’s pass-rush has left much to be desired, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report believes the 49ers should make an all-in move to upgrade the position. Knox recently suggested the 49ers execute a trade with the winless Los Angeles Chargers for Pro Bowler Khalil Mack. “Los Angeles fell to 0-5 on Sunday, while Mack continues to be a legitimate difference-maker,” Knox wrote . “… Mack is playing on a one-year deal and should be interested in playing for a team that could get him his first career playoff win. “.. Mack should be the top target for any team with Super Bowl aspirations that happens to need help rushing opposing passers. It'll be a fairly significant surprise if he remains in Los Angeles beyond next month's deadline.” Despite multiple reports indicating the Chargers would want a fifth-round pick in exchange for Mack, Knox suggested it could take at least a conditional 2027 fourth-round pick to get a deal finalized given the demand for strong pass-rushers from contending teams. Through five games this season, Mack has logged 14 pressures, eight hurries, five tackles for loss, three QB hits, and three sacks with a pass-rush win-rate of 9.5%, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding that kind of production opposite White would be a big boost for the 49ers in the interim, and once Bosa comes back, it would make SF’s pass-rush all the more dangerous come playoff time.

It is time to simply enjoy what the 49ers are doing and stop worrying about their ability to stay healthy. Frankly, they might just win the Super Bowl regardless of who is available. Through five weeks, it feels like their year. Here is how the rest of the Super Bowl race shakes out as the season approaches Week 6. Stock down: Bears desperately await Caleb Williams' return Would the Chicago Bears be 5-0 if Caleb Williams did not get hurt in Week 2? Suppose he stays on the field for that critical fourth-quarter drive in the 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. He would have had at least two more looks at the end zone. If he were available in Week 5, the Bears probably would not throw three interceptions in a 31-7 rout at the hands of the bitter rival Green Bay Packers . That is all hypothetical, of course, but Williams' talent makes it fair to wonder. Instead, the Bears are two games back of the NFC North lead and stand in the middle of the conference's slog of three-win teams. They seek a rebound effort on the heels of the second-worst loss of Ben Johnson's head coaching career. That will be harder to obtain with edge rusher Montez Sweat out for two games for a violation of the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy . The good news (and Chicago needs some right now) is that Williams is on track to play in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons . His hamstring strain is behind him, which cleared the way for a return to practice on Wednesday. Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent kept the ship afloat but had clear limitations — most notably in the frustrating loss to the Packers — whereas Williams seems to be blossoming into a top-tier quarterback capable of leading his team deep into the postseason. It was easy to sneer at the Pittsburgh Steelers in the offseason when they hired a past-his-prime coach, let Aaron Rodgers drag them along with his decision-making process as to whether to return for another year and got embarrassed by the Philadelphia Eagles on draft day. They say everything happens for a reason, and they might be onto something when it comes to the Steelers. All of those developments, somehow, seem to have played out perfectly. San Francisco 49ers Injury Report: Deebo Samuel Timeline, Nick Bosa Updates, and Practice Squad Call-Ups - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL TRENDING Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Savanah Tujague Tue, October 13, 2026 at 3:16 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Fresh off a dramatic 32-29 victory over the Seattle Seahawks to stay perfect at 5-0, the San Francisco 49ers turn their attention to a critical Week 6 home matchup. On Monday, head coach Kyle Shanahan briefed reporters on the team's latest health report, which of course was headlined by another significant blow to the receiving corps alongside potential good news on the defensive front. Deebo Samuel to Miss Time with Hamstring Strain The most concerning news following Sunday's thriller is the loss of wide receiver Deebo Samuel. Samuel suffered a right hamstring strain on an end-around carry in the third quarter, fumbling before remaining on the ground and leaving for the locker room. "He got it pretty good, so he's going to miss some time," Shanahan confirmed Monday. Samuel's absence exacerbates an already thin wide receiver room currently missing Ricky Pearsall, Demarcus Robinson, and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling. With Mike Evans operating through a rib issue, Shanahan noted the team down to just four fully healthy wideouts on the active roster. Rookie Jacob Cowing, who briefly left Sunday's game with an ankle tweak, is expected to be fine. Expect San Francisco to promote a practice squad receiver ahead of Week 6 to restore depth behind Evans and Brandin Cooks. Potential Week 6 Returns: Bosa, Juszczyk, Thompson While the offensive perimeter takes a hit, the 49ers could get key pieces back in time for their showdown with the Washington Commanders. "We know he's got a chance," Shanahan said regarding Bosa's status. "They've all got a chance, but definitely not saying they're good to go right now. We've got to continue to evaluate them throughout the week." Along with Bosa, fullback Kyle Juszczyk (knee) and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. (ankle) are tracking in a similar direction. Both will be tested during practice as the team decides their availability closer to game day. With a 5-0 record and a tight hold on first place in the NFC West, San Francisco's depth continues to be tested. Getting Bosa and Juszczyk back into the fold would provide a timely boost as the 49ers prepare to host the Washington Commanders in their next matchup.
